Huffman pointed directly at Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, features that generate answers and summaries directly inside search results. Rather than sending users to websites to find information, Google increasingly gives them what they are looking for on its own page, pushing traditional search links further down.

Asked whether the changes were responsible for Reddit's declining search traffic, Huffman said the AI features had expanded aggressively in the U.S. and internationally. "The AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," he told investors.

That creates an awkward situation for Reddit—and arguably every other single media site on the internet. People can still search for Reddit discussions, but Google's results increasingly allow them to consume information from those discussions without visiting Reddit itself. Search referrals also bring back existing users, meaning fewer clicks can affect both new-user acquisition and the platform's ability to keep people engaged.

Reddit is trying to reduce that dependence by moving toward a primarily logged-in experience, which would require people to sign into an account before accessing most of the platform. The company plans to begin testing the change in selected markets outside the U.S. during the fourth quarter.

The strategy also connects to Reddit's increasingly important relationship with the AI industry. In February 2024, Reddit signed a reported $60 million-a-year data licensing deal with Google , giving the search giant access to Reddit discussions to train AI models. A few months later, the company announced a similar partnership with OpenAI , allowing the ChatGPT developer to use Reddit content while giving Reddit access to OpenAI's technology.

Those deals turned Reddit's enormous archive of human conversations into something it could sell to AI developers. But the same AI-powered search experience that benefits from Reddit's content can reduce the number of people who actually visit the site. Reddit also started tightening access to its public data and moving toward a more restricted platform which angered long term users.

The stock has now lost 44% over the past week, with Friday's 30.44% plunge accounting for a significant portion of the decline. At $90.15, Reddit is trading well below the levels it held just days ago.

The technical picture offers little immediate relief. Reddit's 50-day exponential moving average, a trend indicator that gives greater weight to recent prices, sits around $149.80, while its 200-day average is near $162.12. The 50-day average has already fallen below the 200-day average, creating a so-called death cross, a bearish signal commonly associated with a longer-term downward trend.

At $90.15, Reddit would need to climb approximately 66%—almost 70%—just to return to its 50-day average. That would only bring the share price back to the shorter-term trend line, not undo the death cross itself. With both averages sitting far above the current price, a recovery to those levels in the near term looks increasingly unlikely.

posts.content:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong and two other insiders filed Rule 10b5-1 plans that let them schedule share sales in advance, with potential sales starting in November 2026 and January 2027.

The filing covers up to 13.59 million Class A shares, and at the October 29 closing price of $160.59, they carry a notional value of about $2.18 billion.

According to the document deposited with the SEC, Armstrong adopted his plan on August 12, and it allows for the sale of as many as 8.1 million shares tied to the exercise of vested stock options, with transactions scheduled to kick off around November 16, 2026, and go on until October 22, 2027, subject to price thresholds in the arrangement.

The second insider looking to liquidate part of their holding is board member Frederick Ernest Ehrsam III, who entered into his plan on September 4. His covers up to 3.8 million Class A shares issuable when Class B shares held by his living trust are converted. Per the filing, the estimated start date is December 7, 2026, with an expiration date of June 7, 2027.

Emilie Choi, Coinbase’s president and chief operating officer, is the third insider mentioned in the document. She adopted her plan a few days after Ehrsam, and it covers the least number of shares of the three, at just over 1.5 million, including stock she owns as well as shares linked to equity awards and stock held by a trust for which her spouse is a co-trustee.

Her window is set to open around January 4, 2027, and closes on the very last day of that year.

The Rule 10b5-1 filing coincided with Coinbase releasing its Q3 2026 results that showed a net income of $719 million, or $2.51 per share, compared to $432.6 million ($1.50 per share) a year earlier.

Transaction revenue went down by 43% to just over $590 million, when last year it had reached $1.05 billion, with prediction markets emerging as a huge growth area for the firm, bringing in more than $200 million in revenue. That area, combined with derivatives, accounted for at least 25% of Coinbase’s total transaction revenue, with subscriptions and services making up 49%.

Additionally, the results showed that total operating expenses between July and September dropped by 17% to $1.15 billion, where it had been about $1.39 billion in the same period in 2025.

Meanwhile, the company’s COIN stock closed yesterday at $160.59 but fell almost 5% to $152.98 in after-hours trading. And as we reported yesterday, the Coinbase stock has fallen by at least 56% from its recent peak, placing it among the weakest performers in a group of major technology companies.

Tether’s excess reserves nearly double to $8B as Q3 profit hits $1.5B

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 The stablecoin issuer’s US Treasury holdings are comparable to those of major foreign holders, while its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion at the end of September.

Tether reported $1.5 billion in third-quarter operating profit as its excess reserves nearly doubled to $7.95 billion, according to figures released alongside its latest attestation prepared by independent accounting firm BDO.

The company held $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities at the end of September, leaving a reserve surplus of $7.95 billion, nearly double the $4.1 billion reported in June. Its assets included $132.4 billion in direct and indirect US Treasury bill holdings.

That exposure is comparable to South Korea’s $134.2 billion in US government debt and exceeds the United Arab Emirates’ $116.1 billion, according to August data from the US Treasury Department.

Tether also generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first nine months of 2026, with income largely driven by US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, according to the company. Its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion, up from approximately $5.8 billion at the end of June.

Tether’s USDT remains the world’s largest stablecoin, accounting for around 60% of the $297.3 billion stablecoin market, according to DefiLlama data . On Friday, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X that USDT’s user base had surpassed 700 million, with adoption concentrated in emerging markets.

The stablecoin issuer has faced years of scrutiny over its reserve transparency. In August, the company announced the completion of its first full independent financial statement audit by KPMG US, although the audited statements were not made public.

Investment gains powered its rebound as prediction markets grew into a $200 million business, while record USDC holdings delivered shrinking revenue after rewards.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Coinbase reported a $719 million Q3 profit as its prediction-market business expanded and crypto investments increased. 02 The exchange added 643 BTC and 2,370 ETH, while prediction markets crossed $200 million in annualized revenue despite weaker spot trading. 03 Record USDC balances failed to prevent a 16.6% decline in revenue remaining after rewards, highlighting the cost of stablecoin growth. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Coinbase returned to a $719 million quarterly profit despite weaker crypto trading, buoyed by its investment gains in Bitcoin.

The exchange's third-quarter earnings , released Oct. 29, showed revenue of $1.216 billion, largely unchanged from the previous quarter but down 35% year over year. Crypto spot trading volume fell 8% to $134.5 billion, while transaction revenue declined 44% from a year earlier to $590 million.

Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas said that Coinbase recorded its 15th consecutive quarter of positive adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, which reached $333 million, up 60% from the previous quarter.

Nevertheless, Coinbase reversed a $359 million second-quarter loss as its diversification strategy gained traction. Prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue, while subscription and services contributed nearly half of net revenue.

The results also revealed growing costs associated with its USDC business and increased investments in Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Prediction markets emerge as Coinbase's fastest-growing business

Coinbase's prediction-market business has emerged as an increasingly important revenue source as sluggish cryptocurrency trading activity weighs on its traditional exchange operations.

According to its Q3 earnings presentation , prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized net revenue during the quarter, following an 82% compound quarterly growth rate since launch.

The company also reported a more than 60% increase in daily prediction-market traders compared with the previous quarter, making the product one of its fastest-growing businesses by revenue.

Coinbase's Prediction Market Annualized Revenue Exceeds $200 Million Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described prediction markets as “one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase history,” highlighting strong demand for cryptocurrency-related event contracts even during seasonally slower sports-betting periods.

The momentum is helping Coinbase diversify its transaction business beyond conventional spot trading.

Prediction markets and derivatives together accounted for approximately 25% of transaction revenue during the quarter, while customers trading event contracts also generated additional cryptocurrency spot trading activity.

These gains helped cushion declining crypto trading volumes. Coinbase's share of global crypto trading activity increased to 10.7% from 5.6% a year earlier, supported by growth across spot and derivatives products.

Meanwhile, subscription and services revenue increased 3% quarter over quarter to $570 million, representing 49% of net revenue.

Haas said the expansion was making Coinbase more resilient because prediction-market revenue was “less correlated to crypto volatility.”

The exchange plans to expand prediction-market engagement through additional event categories and product integrations while developing USDC-native clearing infrastructure to improve trading economics.

“We obtained CFTC approval for our own DCO to support predictions. And so what this means is we have the opportunity to own more of the stack. That means we can launch our own contracts, and we can also then earn better economics.”

Coinbase's record $22 billion USDC holdings conceal growing rewards costs

While prediction markets provided a new growth opportunity, Coinbase's established stablecoin business faced a different financial challenge.

The exchange reported a record $22 billion in average USDC balances across its products, a 49% year-over-year increase and about 30% of the stablecoin's average circulating supply.

However, Coinbase's Q3 filing showed that stablecoin revenue declined 5.4% to $306.9 million from a reclassified $324.5 million a year earlier.

At the same time, USDC rewards expenses increased 15.8% to $129.2 million from $111.6 million, reflecting the growing cost of attracting and retaining stablecoin holders.

Subtracting the disclosed rewards expense from stablecoin revenue leaves approximately $177.7 million, down from $213 million in the comparable quarter.

That represents a $35.3 million decline, or 16.6%, despite the substantial expansion in USDC balances. The calculation excludes other income and expenses associated with the stablecoin business.

The divergence reflects competing pressures on Coinbase's commercial arrangement with Circle, the issuer of USDC.

Coinbase's filing attributed an $84.6 million positive revenue contribution to higher average USDC balances, while lower interest rates created a $52.8 million drag on revenue.

Interest income generated by the reserves backing USDC remains an important component of the economics shared between Coinbase and Circle. Lower rates therefore reduce the revenue available even as more customers hold the stablecoin.

The exchange has also been paying increasingly substantial rewards to support adoption. Still, the firm is looking to attract more participants to the USDC ecosystem. Haas said:

“Circle and we both have a goal to grow overall USDC market cap and adoption. In some cases, we could partner together to bring on more participants into the USDC ecosystem. We could also work independently to partner with various parties and bring them as partners on our respective platforms.”

Coinbase increases Bitcoin and Ethereum investments as crypto prices lift profits

Beyond its expanding trading and stablecoin operations, Coinbase also increased its direct exposure to cryptocurrency markets during the quarter.

A comparison of its second-quarter and third-quarter filings shows that the exchange's Bitcoin holdings for investment increased by 643 BTC, from 17,311 BTC at the end of June to 17,954 BTC in September.

Its Ethereum investment holdings also increased by 2,370 ETH, rising from 150,279 ETH to 152,649 ETH over the same period.

Together with other digital assets, the company's cryptocurrency investment portfolio increased in fair value from $1.47 billion to approximately $2.22 billion, a 51.5% quarterly increase.

Much of that increase reflected higher cryptocurrency valuations, which also contributed significantly to Coinbase's reported profitability.

The exchange recognized approximately $715 million in gains on crypto assets held for investment during the quarter, helping drive its $719 million net profit after three consecutive quarterly losses.

However, adjusted net income, which excludes those investment gains and certain other items, stood at $78 million.

The distinction highlights Coinbase's continued financial exposure to cryptocurrency prices even as prediction markets, stablecoins and subscription services become more prominent sources of revenue.

In its filing, Coinbase estimated that a hypothetical 50% increase or decrease in cryptocurrency prices would change the fair value of its investment portfolio by approximately $1.1 billion, with the resulting gain or loss flowing through its earnings.

Raymond and Isiah Garcia held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for more than nine hours, forcing the father to transfer over $8 million in crypto, in one of the clearest “wrench attack” prosecutions yet.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Judge's gavel. Source: Decrypt/Shutterstock

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Texas brothers Raymond and Isiah Garcia were sentenced to a combined 326 months for a September 2025 home-invasion robbery that forced a Minnesota man to hand over more than $8 million in crypto; both pleaded guilty in June.

The pair zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for over nine hours, even driving the victim to a cabin to retrieve hardware wallets, before fleeing and being arrested near Houston.

Chainalysis logged 46 violent incidents against crypto holders and $30 million-plus stolen in early 2026.

Two Texas brothers have been sentenced to a combined 326 months in prison for a violent home-invasion robbery in which they held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for hours and forced the father to hand over more than $8 million in cryptocurrency.

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced on Thursday to 180 months and 186 months respectively, or 15 and 15-and-a-half years, by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank in St. Paul, according to the Justice Department. Both had pleaded guilty in June.

According to court documents, the brothers traveled from Texas to Grant, Minnesota, and on Sept. 19, 2025, broke into the victim’s home, zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for more than nine hours while demanding access to the father’s crypto accounts.

When he failed to transfer the amount they expected, they forced him to drive one of the brothers to the family’s cabin in upstate Minnesota to retrieve additional hardware wallets and move the funds. In total, they compelled him to transfer over $8 million. The pair fled after the victim’s son called 911, and were later arrested near Houston.

“The Garcia brothers committed a brazen and calculated act of violence against the victim and his family,” U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said in a statement. The FBI’s Christopher Dotson said the brothers “violated the sanctity of a home” in “a brazen act of violence and greed.”

The case is a stark example of a “ wrench attack ,” in which criminals use physical force rather than hacking to seize crypto.

Such attacks have surged alongside crypto’s rising prices: Chainalysis counted 46 violent incidents in the first half of 2026 with more than $30 million stolen, while CertiK pegged losses even higher. Recent cases span a French kidnapping in which workers’ children were held hostage and a UK home invasion that ended in prison terms for the attackers.

The sentencing offers one of the clearest signals yet that U.S. courts are treating crypto wrench attacks as serious violent crime.

Raymond and Isiah Garcia held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for more than nine hours, forcing the father to transfer over $8 million in crypto, in one of the clearest “wrench attack” prosecutions yet.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Texas brothers Raymond and Isiah Garcia were sentenced to a combined 326 months for a September 2025 home-invasion robbery that forced a Minnesota man to hand over more than $8 million in crypto; both pleaded guilty in June.

The pair zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for over nine hours, even driving the victim to a cabin to retrieve hardware wallets, before fleeing and being arrested near Houston.

Chainalysis logged 46 violent incidents against crypto holders and $30 million-plus stolen in early 2026.

Two Texas brothers have been sentenced to a combined 326 months in prison for a violent home-invasion robbery in which they held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for hours and forced the father to hand over more than $8 million in cryptocurrency.

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced on Thursday to 180 months and 186 months respectively, or 15 and 15-and-a-half years, by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank in St. Paul, according to the Justice Department. Both had pleaded guilty in June.

According to court documents, the brothers traveled from Texas to Grant, Minnesota, and on Sept. 19, 2025, broke into the victim’s home, zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for more than nine hours while demanding access to the father’s crypto accounts.

When he failed to transfer the amount they expected, they forced him to drive one of the brothers to the family’s cabin in upstate Minnesota to retrieve additional hardware wallets and move the funds. In total, they compelled him to transfer over $8 million. The pair fled after the victim’s son called 911, and were later arrested near Houston.

“The Garcia brothers committed a brazen and calculated act of violence against the victim and his family,” U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said in a statement. The FBI’s Christopher Dotson said the brothers “violated the sanctity of a home” in “a brazen act of violence and greed.”

The case is a stark example of a “ wrench attack ,” in which criminals use physical force rather than hacking to seize crypto.

Such attacks have surged alongside crypto’s rising prices: Chainalysis counted 46 violent incidents in the first half of 2026 with more than $30 million stolen, while CertiK pegged losses even higher. Recent cases span a French kidnapping in which workers’ children were held hostage and a UK home invasion that ended in prison terms for the attackers.

The sentencing offers one of the clearest signals yet that U.S. courts are treating crypto wrench attacks as serious violent crime.

posts.title: Binance Hack: This Is What Bitcoin Did After 6 Earlier Crypto Disasters
posts.titleVi: Binance Hack: This Is What Bitcoin Did After 6 Earlier Crypto Disasters
posts.summary: The crypto space is still reeling from its biggest hack ever, which saw well over $6 billion worth of crypto drained from Binance, although about $3 billion of that is reported to have been frozen.
posts.summaryVi: The crypto space is still reeling from its biggest hack ever, which saw well over $6 billion worth of crypto drained from Binance, although about $3 billion of that is reported to have been frozen.
posts.content:
The crypto space is still reeling from its biggest hack ever, which saw well over $6 billion worth of crypto drained from Binance, although about $3 billion of that is reported to have been frozen.

The incident affected Bitcoin, which dipped to $76,350 for the first time since mid-September before recovering by a couple of grand. But now, a historical comparison shared by CryptosRus shows that BTC rallied to new all-time highs after several major security failures, leading to the question: will the same happen again this time?

In an October 30 post on X, CryptosRus noted that following the Mt. Gox incident in 2014, the price of Bitcoin initially fell by half but soon embarked on a run that saw it increase a hundredfold by 2017.

Another incident, which happened roughly two years after Mt. Gox, saw nearly 120,000 BTC, valued at about $72 million at the time, stolen from Bitfinex, triggering a 20% dip in the OG cryptocurrency’s value. But as CryptosRus pointed out, it hit a new all-time high near $20,000 almost a year later.

It didn’t stop there. In January 2018, Coincheck, a Japanese crypto exchange, suffered the biggest crypto hack by dollar value at the time, when it lost 523 million NEM tokens valued at about $532 million. Although BTC was not the primary asset stolen, it was still affected, bottoming at around $3,100. But by 2021, it had recorded a new ATH near $69,000.

In the midst of that run to $69K, Binance experienced a major breach where hackers stole over 7,000 BTC worth as much as $41 million on May 7, 2019. Yet again, the asset showed resilience, jumping 136% in just 7 weeks.

While not a hack, CryptosRus included the FTX collapse in 2022, which saw Bitcoin plunge by 22%, before setting off on a run that saw its value skyrocket by about 375%, culminating in a new all-time high just shy of $74,000 in March 2024.

In early 2025, with Bitcoin hitting new highs fueled by the post-US election rally and huge spot ETF flows, Bybit fell victim to a $1.5 billion theft attributed to the Pyongyang-linked Lazarus Group and its affiliate TraderTraitor (which some security experts are blaming for the new Binance heist). In the aftermath of the attack, BTC’s price fell by 24%, but barely three months later, it reached a new record high.

“Bitcoin has survived every one of them,” wrote CryptosRus.

According to Binance, the $6.3 billion hack may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that let an attacker reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. It says it hasn’t found any evidence of a private key leak and that all losses will be covered by its SAFU fund and company money.

Meanwhile, on-chain data shared by CryptoQuant’s Julio Moreno shows that about $3.7 billion of the stolen funds went to one receiver address on Ethereum. Tether and Circle froze $2.2 billion in stablecoins, but that was after the attacker had already sold about $435 million of USDT for ETH through four swap venues.

Per Moreno’s data, the attacker still has around 462,600 ETH, worth about $1.04 billion, under their control, in addition to another $400 million in assorted tokens that they are selling into decentralized pools. According to him, nothing has so far reached a centralized exchange, bridge, or mixer.

As far as Bitcoin is concerned, the thief moved 18,270 BTC valued at about $1.42 billion from Binance’s cold wallet through one staging address and into 19 new ones, with 17 of them holding exactly 1,000 BTC. At the time of writing, the asset had gone back up to just over $78,000, which still represented a drop of over 2% in 24 hours and 6% over 30 days.

Wayne is a dynamic part-time trader with an impressive eye for detail. His passion for understanding financial systems has led to an intriguing interest in blockchain technology, and he enjoys exploring and writing about cryptocurrencies. Possessing a keen intellect and diligent work ethic, he stays up-to-date on the latest industry trends, regularly sharing his insights in articles and professional presentations.

Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3B Binance hack

Markets Published Oct 30, 2026 Circle, Strategy and other crypto-linked stocks fell sharply Friday, a day after Binance disclosed a $6.3 billion security breach.

Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.

Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group ( CRCL ) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy ( MSTR ) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.

The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN ( IREN ), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions ( FIGR ), which dropped about 9%.

The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of a the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record .

Related: Binance working with FBI to recover assets following $6.3B hack

Coinbase and Strategy both reported third-quarter earnings Thursday, with gains on their crypto holdings lifting profits even as revenue declined.

Coinbase reported $719 million in net income, boosted by about $715 million in gains on cryptocurrency investments. Adjusted net income, which excludes investment gains and other items, was $78 million. Net revenue fell about 34% year over year to $1.16 billion.

The exchange also reported that its prediction markets business surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue.

Lagarde to leave ECB with Europe’s tokenized-finance blueprint still undecided

Appia’s consultation findings expose a trade-off between pooling settlement liquidity and preserving competition among networks, with the architecture still open.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Appia received 127 consultation responses and has a blueprint due in 2028. 02 One network could pool liquidity; several could preserve competition but fragment cash and collateral. 03 Pontes targets longer hours by mid-2027 and continuous operation in 2028. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Christine Lagarde will step down as European Central Bank president on Feb. 7, 2027, while the Eurosystem is still weighing how to organize the infrastructure for Europe’s tokenized financial markets through its Appia initiative.

The departure announcement on Oct. 29 comes a day after the Eurosystem published Appia consultation findings that expose a basic tension: concentrating settlement money on one network could make markets more efficient, but concentrating control could make them harder to enter.

Appia is the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop an integrated ecosystem for tokenized wholesale finance, where assets are issued or represented on distributed ledgers. Its new report summarizes 127 responses and leaves the architecture open ahead of a blueprint due by 2028. The findings describe stakeholder views; the Eurosystem has expressed no architecture preference in the report.

Appia’s liquidity pooling meets the access test

Settlement infrastructure determines how buyers pay for assets and how transactions are completed. Appia’s architecture question is where central bank money should be available within a market built across different distributed ledger technology, or DLT, platforms.

Respondents identified advantages to putting settlement on a single network. Concentrated liquidity, common processes and simpler coordination could reduce fragmentation and duplicated investment.

The same arrangement could also concentrate activity in infrastructure with systemic importance. Respondents warned about dependence on a particular technology or vendor and weaker incentives to innovate. Pooling money would therefore solve only part of the integration problem if participants became locked into the platform that held it.

Multiple networks offer a different balance. They can accommodate different business models and reduce dependence on one infrastructure. For a bank, however, competition between platforms could still leave liquidity fragmented if its money or collateral cannot move efficiently between them. Without enforceable interoperability standards, respondents warned, separate networks could divide liquidity, collateral, identity and compliance into new silos.

Related Reading Solana DvP settlement requires 100% upfront cash for every trade

A third configuration would make central bank money available on a limited number of eligible networks, operating under transparent admission criteria and common standards. Many respondents proposed this configuration as a way to balance network choice with common requirements.

That option remains subject to a fundamental test. The report says the feasibility of providing central bank money settlement on more than one network, while preserving Eurosystem control over that money, still needs assessment. An eligible-network model is an option under study, rather than an announced right for operators to connect.

The consultation places access rules at the center of the competition question.

Respondents sought objective, non-discriminatory admission criteria and a clear separation between the shared network and the commercial services built on it. They generally considered client-facing issuance, trading, custody and wallets unsuitable for the shared utility, because those are activities in which providers should compete.

For a DLT operator, that distinction affects whether it supplies common infrastructure, sells services to users, or attempts to do both. The concern is that an operator competing with its own users could undermine the neutrality of the infrastructure they depend on.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The report’s account of respondent views gives greater weight to central bank control, neutrality and open access than to ownership alone. A Eurosystem-operated network and market-operated networks bring different trade-offs; either would need rules that preserve the public authority’s control over central bank money and prevent discriminatory access.

The International Capital Market Association’s April position illustrates the preference for competition at the infrastructure level. It generally favors multiple interoperable networks under harmonized standards over a single Eurosystem-operated network, citing competition, concentration risk and market-led innovation.

That submission reflects a subset of ICMA’s DLT Bonds Working Group and predates the October findings.

For banks, the practical issue is whether settlement balances and collateral can be used efficiently across venues. A common network could concentrate those resources. A competitive network system would need reliable movement between platforms to avoid leaving usable money or assets stranded in separate pools.

The report highlights central bank involvement in liquidity routing and collateral mobilization. Those functions make interoperability an operational requirement, rather than simply an agreement that different technologies should coexist.

Euro stablecoin issuers face a related question about the role of private settlement assets. Respondents viewed tokenized deposits and euro-denominated stablecoins as potentially complementary to central bank money within a two-tier system. That creates a possible place for different payment instruments without making each instrument equivalent to central bank money.

Related Reading How MiCA brings banks closer to controlling Europe’s stablecoin access

Existing collateral policy is narrower than a general opening to on-chain assets. In his Oct. 29 speech , ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said the Eurosystem has accepted marketable assets issued in central securities depositories using DLT since March 30. Whether assets outside currently eligible settlement systems can qualify, and under what criteria, remains under assessment.

Some of the infrastructure is already operating. Pontes launched on Sept. 21 with initial core services and gradual onboarding. It connects market DLT platforms with the Eurosystem’s TARGET Services so wholesale tokenized asset transactions can settle in central bank money.

Cipollone set out the next delivery targets on Oct. 29: significantly longer operating hours by mid-2027 and 24/7/365 availability in 2028. Immediate settlement finality on the Eurosystem DLT platform is planned as early as 2027.

Related Reading ECB launches ‘digital euro for banks’ and prepares to buy tokenized bonds

Appia’s 2028 objective is different: a blueprint containing findings, recommendations and principles for the wider ecosystem. Cipollone also said T2S, the existing securities settlement platform, would continue alongside new tokenized infrastructures.

A leadership handover, with architecture still open

Lagarde’s successor will enter that delivery timetable without acquiring sole authority over the design. Under Article 283 , the European Council appoints the ECB president by qualified majority on a Council recommendation, after consultation with the European Parliament and the ECB Governing Council. The departure release names no successor.

The Governing Council remains the ECB’s main decision-making body, bringing together the Executive Board and euro-area national central bank governors.

The next concrete signals will come from design work and the terms of market participation. The consultation report envisages more complex cross-cutting testing in 2027 and a forthcoming stakeholder call covering tokenized deposits and payments, securities and shared network governance. Participation arrangements are still to be communicated.

For banks, issuers and DLT operators, the eventual access rules will help show whether Europe’s common settlement anchor can support competing businesses without fragmenting the money and collateral they need to operate.

posts.summary: Strategy posted net income of $19.53 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a sharp jump from $2.79 billion a year earlier. The surge came largely from a $20.91 billion gain on its Bitcoin holdings, which pushed operating income to a record high.

posts.content:
Strategy posted net income of $19.53 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a sharp jump from $2.79 billion a year earlier. The surge came largely from a $20.91 billion gain on its Bitcoin holdings, which pushed operating income to a record high.

The company’s revenue, however, moved in the opposite direction and slipped 3% year over year to $125.4 million from $128.7 million. Gross profit was $89.6 million, with a gross margin of 71%, slightly below the $90.7 million reported a year earlier, when the margin was 70%.

Strategy held 848,517 bitcoin as of October 25, with a market value of $68.9 billion against an original cost basis of $64.02 billion. Its average purchase price stood at approximately $75,446 per bitcoin. The company purchased $14.33 billion worth of BTC year-to-date and increased its holdings by 26% during 2026.

But Strategy’s BTC Yield stood at negative 3.7%. Despite this, Michael Saylor, founder and executive chairman of the company, said that “we’re at the beginning of the next bull market.” He went on to add,

“Banks are embracing Bitcoin, Bitcoin’s dominance among digital assets is growing, institutional demand is back, and Bitcoin’s price is 21% above its 200-week moving average. Digital Credit continues to grow, with $16 billion in notional value across ten publicly listed securities. Strategy continues to lead this industry with 84% market share and STRC returning to strength.”

Meanwhile, Strategy appears to have paused its recent BTC buying spree and focused on repurchasing STRC shares instead.

Separately, its Chief Financial Officer Andrew Kang is stepping down on November 5. The exec notified the company earlier this week that he was resigning for personal reasons. Strategy stressed that his departure had nothing to do with any disagreement over its operations, policies, or practices. He will remain available in an advisory role through December 31.

Reza Virasteh, who is currently executive vice president of operations, will take over as co-principal financial officer from January 1, alongside CEO and President Phong Le.

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

Crypto Biz: Bitcoin’s quantum threat is becoming an economic problem

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 Bitcoin faces mounting quantum security concerns as Ripple secures a US banking charter, USDC gains ground in Europe and VanEck adds BTC to a new ETF.

The debate over quantum computing has raised serious questions about Bitcoin’s long-term security, but the economic consequences could emerge long before the technology seriously threatens the network.

Muneeb Ali, founder of Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, believes quantum computing risks are already discouraging institutional investment, even as US spot Bitcoin ETFs have amassed more than $104 billion in net assets, according to BitBo data . He warns that BTC has only a few years to prepare for the transition to quantum-resistant security, a process that could take years given the network’s history of slow and contentious upgrades.

For institutional investors drawn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement , doubts about its long-term security could complicate the investment case.

This week’s Crypto Biz explores the quantum threat, alongside new developments surrounding Ripple, VanEck and European stablecoin adoption.

Bitcoin could face a more serious security challenge if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum resistance by 2028, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network’s lengthy upgrade process leaves little room for delays.

Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Ali said Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap for becoming quantum-resistant, with meaningful progress required by 2028. He cited 2030 as the target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant security, based on guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, though advances in artificial intelligence could bring that deadline forward.

Even if developers agree on how to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks, implementing the changes could take years. Holders would then need time to move their Bitcoin to quantum-resistant addresses.

Although some industry participants dispute the urgency of the threat, Ali argued that uncertainty alone could undermine investor confidence. He also warned that a quantum breakthrough capable of compromising Bitcoin would have consequences for the broader cryptocurrency market.

Ripple has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, clearing the last regulatory hurdle after securing conditional approval in December 2025.

The newly chartered Ripple National Trust Bank will operate under federal supervision, manage reserves backing the company’s RLUSD stablecoin, serve as a collateral trustee for tokenholders and provide digital asset custody. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, which is regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse welcomed the approval, declaring that “crypto and banks work better together.”

The decision follows similar final approval for Circle in July, while Coinbase , Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge remain at the conditional approval stage. Unlike traditional commercial banks, national trust banks generally cannot accept deposits or issue loans and do not carry Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation coverage.

Circle’s USDC has surpassed Tether’s USDt in stablecoin trading against the euro , as European Union regulations reshape competition between the world’s two largest dollar-backed stablecoins.

According to a new report from Kaiko, USDC now accounts for 56% of euro-denominated stablecoin trading, up from just 10% in January 2024. The shift accelerated after major cryptocurrency exchanges restricted USDt trading for European Economic Area customers to comply with the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

USDC’s euro order books are now roughly 40% deeper than USDt’s, suggesting stronger liquidity for traders. However, USDT remains the dominant stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply approximately 2.5 times larger than USDC’s.

The findings come after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the bloc’s first “significant e-money token,” subjecting it to additional regulatory oversight. Kaiko suggested that the US GENIUS Act could produce similar changes in stablecoin trading, depending on how exchanges implement the new requirements.

VanEck, the $244 billion asset manager, has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund that combines traditional stocks and bonds with real assets and a small allocation to Bitcoin.

The VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO), announced Tuesday, invests in a mix of VanEck and third-party ETFs and targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, which can range from 1% to 5%. Rather than holding Bitcoin directly, the fund gains exposure through a spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product. The launch expands VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios into a single ETF.

David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions, said the traditional 60/40 stock-and-bond portfolio was designed for a different investment environment. He contended that adding real assets could help investors navigate a broader range of economic conditions, with Bitcoin now forming a small part of that strategy.

Crypto Biz: Bitcoin’s quantum threat is becoming an economic problem

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 Bitcoin faces mounting quantum security concerns as Ripple secures a US banking charter, USDC gains ground in Europe and VanEck adds BTC to a new ETF.

The debate over quantum computing has raised serious questions about Bitcoin’s long-term security, but the economic consequences could emerge long before the technology seriously threatens the network.

Muneeb Ali, founder of Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, believes quantum computing risks are already discouraging institutional investment, even as US spot Bitcoin ETFs have amassed more than $104 billion in net assets, according to BitBo data . He warns that BTC has only a few years to prepare for the transition to quantum-resistant security, a process that could take years given the network’s history of slow and contentious upgrades.

For institutional investors drawn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement , doubts about its long-term security could complicate the investment case.

This week’s Crypto Biz explores the quantum threat, alongside new developments surrounding Ripple, VanEck and European stablecoin adoption.

Bitcoin could face a more serious security challenge if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum resistance by 2028, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network’s lengthy upgrade process leaves little room for delays.

Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Ali said Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap for becoming quantum-resistant, with meaningful progress required by 2028. He cited 2030 as the target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant security, based on guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, though advances in artificial intelligence could bring that deadline forward.

Even if developers agree on how to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks, implementing the changes could take years. Holders would then need time to move their Bitcoin to quantum-resistant addresses.

Although some industry participants dispute the urgency of the threat, Ali argued that uncertainty alone could undermine investor confidence. He also warned that a quantum breakthrough capable of compromising Bitcoin would have consequences for the broader cryptocurrency market.

Ripple has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, clearing the last regulatory hurdle after securing conditional approval in December 2025.

The newly chartered Ripple National Trust Bank will operate under federal supervision, manage reserves backing the company’s RLUSD stablecoin, serve as a collateral trustee for tokenholders and provide digital asset custody. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, which is regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse welcomed the approval, declaring that “crypto and banks work better together.”

The decision follows similar final approval for Circle in July, while Coinbase , Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge remain at the conditional approval stage. Unlike traditional commercial banks, national trust banks generally cannot accept deposits or issue loans and do not carry Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation coverage.

Circle’s USDC has surpassed Tether’s USDt in stablecoin trading against the euro , as European Union regulations reshape competition between the world’s two largest dollar-backed stablecoins.

According to a new report from Kaiko, USDC now accounts for 56% of euro-denominated stablecoin trading, up from just 10% in January 2024. The shift accelerated after major cryptocurrency exchanges restricted USDt trading for European Economic Area customers to comply with the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

USDC’s euro order books are now roughly 40% deeper than USDt’s, suggesting stronger liquidity for traders. However, USDT remains the dominant stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply approximately 2.5 times larger than USDC’s.

The findings come after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the bloc’s first “significant e-money token,” subjecting it to additional regulatory oversight. Kaiko suggested that the US GENIUS Act could produce similar changes in stablecoin trading, depending on how exchanges implement the new requirements.

VanEck, the $244 billion asset manager, has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund that combines traditional stocks and bonds with real assets and a small allocation to Bitcoin.

The VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO), announced Tuesday, invests in a mix of VanEck and third-party ETFs and targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, which can range from 1% to 5%. Rather than holding Bitcoin directly, the fund gains exposure through a spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product. The launch expands VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios into a single ETF.

David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions, said the traditional 60/40 stock-and-bond portfolio was designed for a different investment environment. He contended that adding real assets could help investors navigate a broader range of economic conditions, with Bitcoin now forming a small part of that strategy.

Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 A recap of Cointelegraph’s live coverage of the Binance hack, including early breach reports and the exchange’s full reimbursement pledge.

This recap summarizes Cointelegraph’s reporting on the Binance hack and has been updated with the exchange’s latest statements. The investigation is ongoing, and figures and recovery timelines may change. See our archived live coverage for the original timeline.

Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Thursday, in what is now the largest cryptocurrency theft on record . Industry partners have frozen roughly $3 billion in affected assets, while customers await the reopening of withdrawals.

TRM Labs traced the first unauthorized transfers to around 8:05 pm UTC Thursday, with Binance wallets drained across multiple blockchains. The attackers targeted hot wallets, which exchanges keep connected to the internet to process withdrawals.

TRM attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. Binance has not publicly confirmed the attackers’ identity.

“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” said Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

Binance said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the affected tokens. However, that allocation excludes the frozen assets, and the exchange said it was buying the remaining tokens through exchanges and over-the-counter deals.

A spokesperson told Cointelegraph the $5 billion was in Binance’s custody but declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security concerns. Security firm CertiK said it needed more information to verify the holdings independently.

Frozen funds are not necessarily recovered funds, and Binance has yet to disclose how much stolen crypto has actually been returned to its control.

Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade came under fire after attackers used it to drain a Binance wallet. EIP-7702 is a feature that lets a wallet authorize software to act on its behalf. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph that compromised signing systems likely enabled the theft.

Attackers could have stolen the funds without EIP-7702, but it may have helped them bypass safeguards and drain assets in one sweep, Ben-Natan said.

Teng said that the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to gain execution authority over a hot wallet without passing Binance’s normal approval controls. A “self-destruct mechanism” destroyed tools and traces, complicating the investigation, he said.

Binance said investigators had also uncovered additional breaches beyond the initially suspected compromised laptop. However, it reported no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked and said it expected to share further technical findings within about 48 hours.

Chainalysis observed thousands of transactions in quick succession that could indicate automated laundering, with funds circulating among addresses and sometimes returning to wallets used earlier.

The theft rattled crypto prices and prompted a precautionary freeze on new deposits and borrowing at decentralized lender Aave. Aave reopened its markets Friday afternoon, while Binance’s withdrawals remained suspended.

Binance said in a Friday update that it aimed to begin reopening withdrawals in stages Sunday, Nov. 1, subject to completing security checks. Deposits and other unaffected services remained operational.

The exchange said it planned to take an initial proof-of-reserves snapshot within 12 hours of the announcement, with results ready by Monday. The report is intended to show the assets Binance holds and the backing of customer balances.

Decrypt News Business Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Cover Hack Losses, CEO Says 'Your Assets Are Safe'

Richard Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism and an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Binance CEO Richard Teng. Image: Binance/Decrypt (CC BY 4.0)

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange will cover all hacked losses, having reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds, $5 billion in the affected tokens.

Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism to wipe tooling and traces, and an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.

Binance aims to restore withdrawals by Sunday and publish a full proof of reserves by Monday, as the attacker keeps moving funds on Tron.

Binance will cover every dollar lost in this week's hack with its own money, CEO Richard Teng said in a video address on Friday, adding that customer funds were never touched.

"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said, according to a transcript he tweeted.

An update on the security incident. pic.twitter.com/qn2804fO5z

— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) October 30, 2026

Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens taken, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB, he said. The exchange is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels.

Teng said the hack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. "We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," he said, adding that most user assets are held in cold wallets and only moved into a hot wallet when a user withdraws. Binance's ability to absorb a loss of this size comes from keeping much of its operating earnings in crypto, he said.

Binance had earlier said it would cover all losses from its SAFU emergency fund and company funds.

Teng said the hack "was not carried out by one person." Binance initially traced it to a compromised laptop but has since found additional points of breach. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces along the way, making the attack harder to investigate, Teng said.

The attacker used EIP-7702 , an Ethereum feature that lets standard wallets run smart contract code, to obtain onchain execution approval over a hot wallet, according to Teng. "That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls," he said, which is why Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and retest its infrastructure. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the theft to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.

Binance hopes to restore withdrawals before its Sunday deadline, Teng said, and is carrying out a full security review covering endpoints, cloud, key management and signing. It plans to publish a full proof of reserves report by Monday, with an initial view before then.

The attacker is still moving funds. Between 11:37 a.m. and 12:12 p.m. ET on Friday, a Tron wallet that Arkham attributes to the hacker sent about 5.19 million TRX, worth roughly $1.73 million, to 12 addresses, according to Arkham data .

All markets are now unfrozen across Aave V3 and V4.

They were frozen as a precaution after initial reports, which paused new deposits and borrows while withdrawals and repayments continued as normal.

Decentralized lending protocol Aave, where the attacker borrowed ETH against USDT while racing stablecoin freezes, according to TRM Labs , said on Friday that it had unfrozen all markets on its V3 and V4 deployments. It had frozen them as a precaution after the first reports of the hack, pausing new deposits and borrowing while withdrawals and repayments continued. Decrypt News Business Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Cover Hack Losses, CEO Says 'Your Assets Are Safe'

Richard Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism and an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Binance CEO Richard Teng. Image: Binance/Decrypt (CC BY 4.0)

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange will cover all hacked losses, having reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds, $5 billion in the affected tokens.

Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism to wipe tooling and traces, and an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.

Binance aims to restore withdrawals by Sunday and publish a full proof of reserves by Monday, as the attacker keeps moving funds on Tron.

Binance will cover every dollar lost in this week's hack with its own money, CEO Richard Teng said in a video address on Friday, adding that customer funds were never touched.

"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said, according to a transcript he tweeted.

An update on the security incident. pic.twitter.com/qn2804fO5z

— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) October 30, 2026

Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens taken, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB, he said. The exchange is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels.

Teng said the hack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. "We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," he said, adding that most user assets are held in cold wallets and only moved into a hot wallet when a user withdraws. Binance's ability to absorb a loss of this size comes from keeping much of its operating earnings in crypto, he said.

Binance had earlier said it would cover all losses from its SAFU emergency fund and company funds.

Teng said the hack "was not carried out by one person." Binance initially traced it to a compromised laptop but has since found additional points of breach. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces along the way, making the attack harder to investigate, Teng said.

The attacker used EIP-7702 , an Ethereum feature that lets standard wallets run smart contract code, to obtain onchain execution approval over a hot wallet, according to Teng. "That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls," he said, which is why Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and retest its infrastructure. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the theft to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.

Binance hopes to restore withdrawals before its Sunday deadline, Teng said, and is carrying out a full security review covering endpoints, cloud, key management and signing. It plans to publish a full proof of reserves report by Monday, with an initial view before then.

The attacker is still moving funds. Between 11:37 a.m. and 12:12 p.m. ET on Friday, a Tron wallet that Arkham attributes to the hacker sent about 5.19 million TRX, worth roughly $1.73 million, to 12 addresses, according to Arkham data .

All markets are now unfrozen across Aave V3 and V4.

They were frozen as a precaution after initial reports, which paused new deposits and borrows while withdrawals and repayments continued as normal.

Decentralized lending protocol Aave, where the attacker borrowed ETH against USDT while racing stablecoin freezes, according to TRM Labs , said on Friday that it had unfrozen all markets on its V3 and V4 deployments. It had frozen them as a precaution after the first reports of the hack, pausing new deposits and borrowing while withdrawals and repayments continued. "Aave was unaffected, and all positions remain overcollateralized," founder Stani Kulechov wrote .

Binance co-founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao said that while the $6.3 billion theft is the largest in dollar terms, it is not the largest in Bitcoin terms, pointing to Mt. Gox's loss of 650,000 BTC, more than 5% of the supply. Unlike at Mt. Gox and FTX, where nearly all users were affected, Binance is covering the losses itself, he said. "It hurts, but we survive," Zhao wrote.

MEXC bất ngờ rút khỏi 4 quốc gia dù tham vọng cạnh tranh với các sàn giao dịch hàng đầu thế giới

Sàn crypto MEXC thông báo sẽ từng bước ngừng cung cấp dịch vụ cho người dùng tại Pháp , đánh dấu thị trường thứ tư mà sàn rút lui kể từ cuối tháng 9.

Theo thông báo ngày 28/10, MEXC sẽ bắt đầu áp dụng các hạn chế theo từng nhóm người dùng từ ngày 18/11 .

Các vị thế còn mở sẽ được tự động đóng vào ngày 22/1/2027 , trong khi hạn cuối để người dùng rút tài sản khỏi nền tảng là ngày 5/3/2027 .

Những tài sản còn lại sau thời hạn này dự kiến được chuyển sang một đơn vị lưu ký được quản lý, nhưng MEXC hiện chưa công bố danh tính bên tiếp nhận.

Trước Pháp, MEXC đã thông báo ngừng dịch vụ tại Hà Lan vào ngày 29/9 , sau đó tiếp tục rút khỏi Nga và Belarus ngày 20/10.

Động thái tại Pháp đáng chú ý hơn khi cơ quan quản lý tài chính AMF từng đưa MEXC vào danh sách cảnh báo từ tháng 6/2024 vì cung cấp dịch vụ mà không có giấy phép cần thiết.

Việc MiCA được triển khai rộng hơn tại châu Âu cũng khiến các sàn crypto phải đáp ứng yêu cầu cấp phép và tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt hơn.

MEXC cho biết người dùng Pháp sẽ chỉ có thể giảm hoặc đóng vị thế sau khi hạn chế có hiệu lực.

MEXC is withdrawing from France, its fourth country exit since September.

French users face automatic position closures on Jan. 22, 2027, and withdrawals end March 5.

— CryptoSlate (@CryptoSlate) October 30, 2026

MEXC vẫn muốn mở rộng sang nhiều loại tài sản

Dù rút khỏi một số thị trường, CEO Vugar Usi vẫn đang theo đuổi chiến lược mở rộng MEXC từ một sàn crypto tập trung nhiều vào memecoin sang nền tảng giao dịch đa tài sản.

MEXC hiện cho biết có khoảng 40 triệu người dùng , hơn 90% là khách hàng cá nhân.

Trong tháng 9, khối lượng giao dịch cổ phiếu Mỹ token hóa tăng 81% , còn nhóm cổ phiếu và ETF token hóa liên quan đến AI tăng 88% .

Sàn cũng đang cung cấp hơn 450 cặp futures cổ phiếu và chỉ số , cùng hơn 200 cổ phiếu Mỹ token hóa.

Tuy nhiên, việc liên tục rút khỏi các thị trường cho thấy tham vọng mở rộng toàn cầu của MEXC vẫn phải đối mặt với áp lực pháp lý ngày càng lớn , đặc biệt tại châu Âu.

CZ nhắn Elon Musk ngừng trêu chọc, tiết lộ lượng cổ phần SpaceX “của chúng ta” vượt 1 tỷ USD

Trong lúc Binance xử lý hậu quả vụ hack lớn ngày 30/10, đồng sáng lập Changpeng Zhao (CZ) bất ngờ nhắc tới lượng cổ phần SpaceX mà ông cho rằng Binance đang nắm giữ.

CZ cho biết khoản đầu tư này có liên quan đến 500 triệu USD Binance từng rót vào thương vụ Elon Musk mua Twitter , và hiện số cổ phần SpaceX tương ứng có giá trị hơn 1 tỷ USD .

Thông tin về quyền sở hữu, giá trị và mối liên hệ giữa khoản đầu tư Twitter với cổ phần SpaceX hiện chủ yếu dựa trên tuyên bố của CZ.

Trong một trao đổi với Elon Musk, CZ cũng đề nghị tỷ phú này ngừng “troll” trong thời điểm Binance đang xử lý khủng hoảng.

Yi He: Binance chưa cần bán cổ phần SpaceX

Đồng sáng lập Binance Yi He cho biết doanh thu trong năm của công ty đủ để bù đắp thiệt hại , nên Binance hiện chưa cần bán lượng cổ phần SpaceX nói trên.

CZ sau đó giải thích rằng ông chỉ muốn cho Musk thấy Binance vẫn có những tài sản giá trị lớn mà vị tỷ phú này có thể dễ dàng nhận biết.

Tuy nhiên, cần phân biệt rằng doanh thu hằng năm không đồng nghĩa với lượng tiền mặt có thể sử dụng ngay , còn giá trị cổ phần SpaceX cũng không phải tiền mặt cho tới khi được bán hoặc chuyển nhượng.

Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop.

Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion.

Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026

Binance dành hơn 6 tỷ USD để xử lý thiệt hại

Trong cập nhật riêng, Binance cho biết đã dành hơn 6 tỷ USD nguồn lực của công ty để bù đắp tổn thất từ vụ hack .

Trong số này, khoảng 5 tỷ USD đã được nắm giữ dưới dạng chính các token bị ảnh hưởng , còn phần thiếu hụt đang được mua thêm qua thị trường và các giao dịch OTC.

Binance cho biết quá trình này có thể kéo dài do một số token có thanh khoản hạn chế.

Con số trên không bao gồm khoảng 3 tỷ USD tài sản bị đánh cắp đã được đóng băng , vì số tài sản này vẫn đang trong quá trình xác minh và thu hồi.

Do đó, việc Binance có thể bù đắp thiệt hại hiện dựa trên nhiều nguồn lực khác nhau, thay vì chỉ phụ thuộc vào lượng cổ phần SpaceX mà CZ đề cập.

posts.titleVi: Binance Hacked for $6.3B, Fed Holds Rates, Bitcoin Crashes to 6-Week Low: Weekly Crypto Recap
posts.summary: Although all crypto eyes were on the Federal Reserve FOMC meeting on Wednesday and a few other major macro events, none of those were the moment of the week. But first, let’s see how the week actually unfolded, starting from our previous market update from last Friday.
posts.summaryVi: Although all crypto eyes were on the Federal Reserve FOMC meeting on Wednesday and a few other major macro events, none of those were the moment of the week. But first, let’s see how the week actually unfolded, starting from our previous market update from last Friday.
posts.content:
Although all crypto eyes were on the Federal Reserve FOMC meeting on Wednesday and a few other major macro events, none of those were the moment of the week.

But first, let’s see how the week actually unfolded, starting from our previous market update from last Friday. At the time, BTC was fighting to stay above the key $80,000 support after getting rejected at $85,000, and investors braced for the FOMC meeting. Somewhat surprisingly, BTC dipped to a five-week low on Saturday at $79,100 before rebounding $2,000 on Sunday.

However, it couldn’t really maintain its position above $80,000 and dipped on a few more occasions by Tuesday. The bulls went on a mild run ahead of the FOMC meeting, pushing the asset to $81,700. It dipped before the meeting and jumped again to $81,800 after the central bank paused interest rate hikes as expected.

Another rejection followed, and BTC dropped to $80,500 on Thursday. The real impact came a day later, early on Friday morning, when reports emerged that the world’s largest crypto exchange had fallen victim to a major hack. Later on, the company confirmed the news, while on-chain data showed that the losses were somewhere around $6.3 billion, even though several entities, including Tether, froze roughly $3 billion.

This became by far the largest hack in the crypto industry. Naturally, bitcoin and almost all alts tanked, with the leading crypto asset dropping to a six-week low of $76,400 before rebounding by a grand. BNB dumped below $700, while SOL has slumped by over 7%. The liquidations skyrocketed to $1.5 billion, while the number of wiped-out traders jumped to over 235,000 on a daily scale.

Market Cap: $2.690T | 24H Vol: $152B | BTC Dominance: 57.8%

BTC: $77,380 (-5.1%) | ETH: $2,225 (-7.4%) | XRP: $1.25 (-4.5%)

Ripple Clears Final OCC Hurdle for National Trust Bank . Ripple had a massive week, and perhaps the OCC approval stands out at the top. Company CEO Brad Garlinghouse announced that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted the final green light for the establishment of Ripple National Trust Bank.

Your Trezor Could Be Compromised: Company Issues Urgent Warning to Customers . One of the leading hardware wallet manufacturers warned customers who bought some of its devices from CryptoBilis on or after March 2026 to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible.

Polymarket Trading Disrupted After Users Report $2.6M in Losses . Hours before the massive Binance hack, Polymarket admitted that bad actors drained over $2.6 million from user accounts. The platform went into cancel-only mode for a while, and Polymarket said an external provider was compromised, not its internal infrastructure.

Bitcoin Sees Biggest Exchange Outflow in Five Weeks Ahead of Fed Decision . In just a single day before the key FOMC meeting, on-chain data showed that bitcoin investors had withdrawn almost 15,000 units from exchanges. The company said this was the largest daily net outflow in five weeks.

Strive Makes Largest-Ever Bitcoin Purchase With 6,182 BTC Buy . The Matt Cole-led company announced its most significant bitcoin purchase to date, accumulating 6,182 units for over $510 million. Meanwhile, the largest corporate holder of the cryptocurrency stood on the sidelines.

HYPE Price Rises 15% Following NYSE Plan to Bring Hyperliquid Perps to the US . Although most altcoins are deep in the red this week, the graph above shows that HYPE has clearly defied that trend. Although all crypto eyes were on the Federal Reserve FOMC meeting on Wednesday and a few other major macro events, none of those were the moment of the week.

But first, let’s see how the week actually unfolded, starting from our previous market update from last Friday. At the time, BTC was fighting to stay above the key $80,000 support after getting rejected at $85,000, and investors braced for the FOMC meeting. Somewhat surprisingly, BTC dipped to a five-week low on Saturday at $79,100 before rebounding $2,000 on Sunday.

However, it couldn’t really maintain its position above $80,000 and dipped on a few more occasions by Tuesday. The bulls went on a mild run ahead of the FOMC meeting, pushing the asset to $81,700. It dipped before the meeting and jumped again to $81,800 after the central bank paused interest rate hikes as expected.

Another rejection followed, and BTC dropped to $80,500 on Thursday. The real impact came a day later, early on Friday morning, when reports emerged that the world’s largest crypto exchange had fallen victim to a major hack. Later on, the company confirmed the news, while on-chain data showed that the losses were somewhere around $6.3 billion, even though several entities, including Tether, froze roughly $3 billion.

This became by far the largest hack in the crypto industry. Naturally, bitcoin and almost all alts tanked, with the leading crypto asset dropping to a six-week low of $76,400 before rebounding by a grand. BNB dumped below $700, while SOL has slumped by over 7%. The liquidations skyrocketed to $1.5 billion, while the number of wiped-out traders jumped to over 235,000 on a daily scale.

BTC: $77,380 (-5.1%) | ETH: $2,225 (-7.4%) | XRP: $1.25 (-4.5%)

Ripple Clears Final OCC Hurdle for National Trust Bank . Ripple had a massive week, and perhaps the OCC approval stands out at the top. Company CEO Brad Garlinghouse announced that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted the final green light for the establishment of Ripple National Trust Bank.

Your Trezor Could Be Compromised: Company Issues Urgent Warning to Customers . One of the leading hardware wallet manufacturers warned customers who bought some of its devices from CryptoBilis on or after March 2026 to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible.

Polymarket Trading Disrupted After Users Report $2.6M in Losses . Hours before the massive Binance hack, Polymarket admitted that bad actors drained over $2.6 million from user accounts. The platform went into cancel-only mode for a while, and Polymarket said an external provider was compromised, not its internal infrastructure.

Bitcoin Sees Biggest Exchange Outflow in Five Weeks Ahead of Fed Decision . In just a single day before the key FOMC meeting, on-chain data showed that bitcoin investors had withdrawn almost 15,000 units from exchanges. The company said this was the largest daily net outflow in five weeks.

Strive Makes Largest-Ever Bitcoin Purchase With 6,182 BTC Buy . The Matt Cole-led company announced its most significant bitcoin purchase to date, accumulating 6,182 units for over $510 million. Meanwhile, the largest corporate holder of the cryptocurrency stood on the sidelines.

Decrypt News Business Elon Musk, CZ Trade Blows Over SpaceX Shares After $6.4B Binance Hack

After Musk appeared to mock Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, CZ reminded him that the exchange’s $500 million bet on his Twitter takeover is now worth over $1 billion in SpaceX shares.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Elon Musk and Changpeng "CZ" Zhao. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

CZ asked Elon Musk to stop trolling Binance over its $6.3 billion hack, citing the exchange's SpaceX shares, which he values at more than $1 billion.

Binance co-CEO Yi He said the company's annual revenue is sufficient to cover the losses without selling its SpaceX holdings. CZ later clarified that he had never suggested selling the shares.

Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, while TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, better known as CZ, called out Elon Musk on Friday after the billionaire appeared to mock the exchange following a $6.4 billion hack—the largest in history—reminding him that Binance holds SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

"Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," CZ wrote on X. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!"

The exchange followed Musk's response to a post estimating that, as a lot of the stolen funds have been frozen, Binance's losses could reach around $1 billion, despite holding approximately $144 billion in assets under custody.

Musk had replied to the discussion with a grimacing emoji, prompting another user to share an old post from former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried claiming his exchange had enough money to cover its losses. FTX famously collapsed weeks later.

Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop.

Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion.

Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026

CZ had initially responded to the loss estimate by saying the damage might be somewhat higher but that Binance would still be able to cover it. Musk's emoji appeared to draw an uncomfortable parallel with the FTX episode, although he did not elaborate on what he meant.

Of course, CZ didn't imply anything else about what Binance may do with its SpaceX shares.

Binance co-CEO Yi He also joined the exchange, addressing CZ in a post that appeared to respond to the suggestion that the company might need to liquidate its SpaceX holdings.

"Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company's revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on," she wrote, adding a shrugging emoji.

CZ subsequently clarified that he had never suggested selling the shares. He said he was simply showing Musk some of the funds Binance had available, hoping to reassure him about the exchange's financial position.

😂 did say anything about selling SPCX shares, was just saying/showing some funds that he might know, so that he can be less worried.

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026

The argument comes as Binance deals with the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. At least $6.4 billion in crypto was taken from wallets associated with the exchange on Thursday, October 29, across multiple blockchains.

Just yesterday, initial reports showed that at least $5.57 billion had left Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Bitcoin, and Tron. The attackers moved funds through several transactions, including a transfer of more than $1.6 billion in USDT to a newly created Ethereum address.

The incident also exposed an important weakness in how cryptocurrency can be recovered after a theft. Tether and Circle, the companies behind the USDT and USDC stablecoins, froze approximately $1.8 billion in assets associated with the attackers in the initial response, then subsequently froze a total of $2.39 billion. Unlike those tokens, Ethereum cannot be frozen by a central issuer, making it harder to stop stolen funds once they are converted.

→ Buy Bitcoin with USDT Powered by Jupiter

Price data by CoinGecko CoinGecko More Bitcoin news and projections →

The attackers subsequently used decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and lending protocol Aave to move funds into Ethereum. These platforms allow users to trade or borrow cryptocurrency without relying on a traditional intermediary to approve each transaction. Decrypt tracked wallets receiving tens of thousands of ETH through these operations, including 19,762 ETH borrowed against approximately $60 million in USDT.

The suspected attackers have also been linked to North Korea. In a Friday report , blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group previously blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. Chainalysis estimated the Binance theft at approximately $6.4 billion.

Binance has since said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, including $5 billion already held in the same tokens that were stolen. The exchange said it is acquiring the remaining assets through market and over-the-counter purchases, which can take longer when certain tokens have limited liquidity.
