posts.content:
Dữ liệu tiền điện tử bị rò rỉ ảnh hưởng đến nhà cung cấp Coinbase và Bithumb: Người dùng có thể bảo vệ tài khoản của mình như thế nào?

Vấn nạn rò rỉ dữ liệu tiền điện tử lại một lần nữa trở thành tâm điểm chú ý sau bốn vụ việc được báo cáo liên quan đến các sàn giao dịch tiền điện tử và các công ty tài chính Hàn Quốc.

Theo một bài đăng trên X của CZ, nhà cung cấp Amplitude của Coinbase đã để lộ thông tin liên lạc của một số người dùng, trong khi sàn giao dịch Bithumb của Hàn Quốc cũng gặp phải sự cố rò rỉ dữ liệu người dùng. Hai công ty chứng khoán truyền thống, Mirae Asset và Daishin Securities, cũng được cho là bị ảnh hưởng.

Những sự việc này làm nổi bật một thực tế khó chịu: bảo vệ tiền của khách hàng là chưa đủ khi thông tin cá nhân rơi vào tay kẻ xấu.

Bốn vụ rò rỉ dữ liệu được báo cáo làm dấy lên lo ngại về an ninh

Các sự cố được báo cáo liên quan đến cả dịch vụ tiền điện tử và tài chính truyền thống. Mặc dù sự cố với nhà cung cấp Coinbase được cho là đã làm lộ thông tin liên hệ, nhưng tiền trong tài khoản được cho là không bị ảnh hưởng.

Tuy nhiên, việc rò rỉ tên, địa chỉ email, số điện thoại, địa chỉ nhà, giấy tờ tùy thân và lịch sử giao dịch có thể tạo ra những rủi ro nghiêm trọng. Tội phạm có thể sử dụng thông tin này để lừa đảo trực tuyến, đánh cắp SIM và tấn công phi kỹ thuật. Trong một số trường hợp, thông tin cá nhân và tài sản bị lộ cũng có thể làm tăng nguy cơ tống tiền ngoài đời thực.

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected). 2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 3. Mirae Asset 4. Daishin Securities

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 28, 2026

Hãy bảo mật tài khoản tiền điện tử của bạn trước khi gặp rắc rối

Hãy bắt đầu từ những điều cơ bản. Sử dụng một địa chỉ email riêng biệt cho mỗi lần trao đổi, tránh chia sẻ thông tin cá nhân không cần thiết và cân nhắc sử dụng một số điện thoại riêng cho các tài khoản tài chính.

Trình quản lý mật khẩu có thể tạo ra các mật khẩu mạnh và độc nhất. Để xác thực mạnh hơn, hãy sử dụng khóa bảo mật phần cứng, passkey hoặc ứng dụng xác thực thay vì xác thực hai yếu tố dựa trên SMS.

Nếu có thể, hãy bật tính năng cho phép rút tiền theo danh sách trắng, khóa thời gian rút tiền và mã chống lừa đảo. Thường xuyên xem xét các phiên hoạt động và khóa API, xóa các khóa không sử dụng và hạn chế quyền truy cập API cần thiết theo địa chỉ IP.

Người dùng tiền điện tử nên làm gì sau các vụ xâm phạm dữ liệu?

Đừng bao giờ tin tưởng những tin nhắn không được yêu cầu gửi đến, tự xưng là cung cấp dịch vụ khôi phục tài khoản hoặc hỗ trợ bảo mật khẩn cấp. Nhân viên hỗ trợ Exchange chính thức sẽ không yêu cầu mật khẩu, mã xác thực hoặc cụm từ khôi phục. Hãy truy cập trực tiếp trang web của Exchange thay vì nhấp vào các liên kết trong email hoặc tin nhắn.

Nếu có thông báo về vi phạm bảo mật, hãy thay đổi mật khẩu bị ảnh hưởng, thu hồi các phiên và khóa API đáng ngờ, xem xét lại các khoản rút tiền và kiểm tra xem email của bạn có xuất hiện trên trang Have I Been Pwned hay không.

Việc rò rỉ dữ liệu tiền điện tử không tự động có nghĩa là tiền của bạn bị xâm phạm . Nhưng việc tăng cường bảo mật tài khoản và giảm thiểu thông tin cá nhân bị lộ có thể khiến cuộc chiến của kẻ tấn công trở nên khó khăn hơn đáng kể.

posts.titleVi: Bitcoin Reclaims $81K Ahead of FOMC Meeting, M Pumps by 12%: Market Watch
posts.summary: Bitcoin’s price has soared by around $2,000 over the past day as markets are preparing for the second-to-last US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting of the year later today. The altcoins have turned green as well, with ETH nearing $2,400 and XRP reclaiming the key $1.30 support.
posts.summaryVi: Bitcoin’s price has soared by around $2,000 over the past day as markets are preparing for the second-to-last US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting of the year later today. The altcoins have turned green as well, with ETH nearing $2,400 and XRP reclaiming the key $1.30 support.
posts.content:
Bitcoin’s price has soared by around $2,000 over the past day as markets are preparing for the second-to-last US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting of the year later today.

The altcoins have turned green as well, with ETH nearing $2,400 and XRP reclaiming the key $1.30 support. BTW and PEPE have rocketed once again.

The primary cryptocurrency faced a sharp rejection precisely a week ago when the bulls managed to push it to a 14-day peak of $85,000. However, that was short-lived, and the asset quickly tumbled by over two grand. The adverse price developments intensified as the week progressed, and BTC was close to breaking below $80,000 by Friday.

Although it defended that level at first, the bears ultimately broke past it on Saturday when bitcoin tanked to a 5-week low of $79,100. It tried to rebound on Sunday but was halted at $81,000 and dipped below $80,000 on a couple more occasions.

The beginning of the current business week didn’t provide the necessary relief rally, and BTC stood below $80,000 for a while. Interestingly, it shot up earlier today to over $80,000, while the bulls initiated another leg up minutes ago to $81,650. Bitcoin remains at around $81,500 as of press time, but more volatility is expected today after the conclusion of the FOMC meeting and the subsequent Kevin Warsh speech.

For now, its market cap has risen to $1.630 trillion, while its dominance over the alts has reclaimed the 60% line on CMC.

Ethereum is up by 3% in the past day and now sits close to $2,400 again. BNB is above $750, while XRP’s 3% pump has pushed it further above the crucial $1.30 support. SOL has rebounded from its sub-$100 dip, while HYPE, DOGE, XMR, and LINK have posted gains of up to 5%.

ZEC, NEAR, and BCH are the most impressive gainers out of the top 15-20 alts. BTW has soared by almost 30%, followed by PEPE’s 16% rise and M’s 12% jump.

The cumulative market cap of all crypto assets has regained over $40 billion in a day and now sits above $2.710 trillion on CMC.

Markets Here's how much bitcoin and the S&P 500 could rally after midterms

Both bitcoin and the S&P 500 have historically produced positive returns in a year after midterms. BTC's pattern, however, could also be explained by the four-year halving cycles.

By Omkar Godbole Updated Oct 28, 2026, 5:46 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 5:15 a.m. EDT

3 min read Make preferred on Share 

Bitcoin's performance one year after previous U.S. midterm elections. (CoinDesk, TradingView) Підсумок Показати Bitcoin gained an average of 53.7% in the 12 months after the past three U.S. midterm elections, excluding 2010, though its four-year halving cycle may better explain those rallies. The S&P 500 has risen an average of 15.17 percent in the year after midterm elections since 1950, more than double its average gain in other years. A Democratic takeover of at least one chamber of Congress could intensify disputes over federal debt, defense spending and President Donald Trump’s crypto ties, although markets have largely priced in divided government.

Both crypto and Wall Street could be in for a strong run after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, if history is a guide.

Since its inception in 2009, bitcoin BTC $80 690,83 , the largest cryptocurrency by market value, has seen four midterms. Leaving out 2010, when the market was tiny and fringe, the other three saw prices for the cryptocurrency rise an average of 53.7% in the 12 months after Election Day, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk. The returns here refer to the percentage rise from the daily close (00:00 UTC) on Election Day to the close on the same date a year later.

Bitcoin surged 1,579% in the 12 months after the 2010 midterm, but the market was fringe and too small then for that figure to be reliable.

If history repeats, bitcoin’s recent subdued price action around $80,000 could pave the way for another leg higher after Nov. 3. BTC has already bounced more than 35% since bottoming out below $60,000 in June. Some analysts believe now is the time to buy and hold crypto , as a new bull run is upon us.

Still, history is too limited to draw firm conclusions, and the post-midterm surges in BTC seen over the years may have more to do with the four-year cycle than U.S. politics.

Bitcoin tends to move in cycles of roughly four years, built around the mining reward halving, an inbuilt code in the Bitcoin blockchain that reduces the per block BTC produced and given to miners by 50% every four years.

After each of the four halvings to date, BTC rallied sharply, peaked 12 to 18 months later and then sliding into a bear market. Those bear markets played out in midterm years – 2014, 2018, 2022 and now 2026. So the rebound that followed the midterms may have been a fresh cycle start rather than politics at work.

The S&P 500 has a much longer record, and it also points up, a positive sign for bitcoin and other risk assets.

Since 1950, the index has averaged a 15.17% gain in the year after midterms, against 7.30% in all other years, according to Hartford Funds.

The 2026 elections could change how President Donald Trump operates in his final two years in the White House.

If Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress, the politics over the record federal debt may heat up, as the debt limit issue is still unresolved and talks over the same may complicate. Trump’s push for $350 billion in mandatory defense funding may not stand a chance, according to Brookings . Democrats could use legislative hurdles to arrest funding for Middle East escalations.

Speaking of crypto, Democratic committee chairs could investigate conflicts of interest tied to Trump’s personal crypto profits. Democratic lawmakers have already sent oversight letters on the president’s crypto ties and family business ventures. Trump’s memecoin, launched in January 2025, has also led to heavy losses for retail investors .

That said, the Supreme Court’s ruling in Trump v. Slaughter left most financial regulators under White House control, so Congress could do little to stop the administration from promoting crypto.

For now, markets have largely priced in a divided federal government , with Democrats expected to retake at least one chamber of Congress.

Finance Securitize adds Stellar blockchain as institutional tokenization gathers steam

The firms announced the agreement at Meridian 2026, the Stellar Development Foundation’s annual conference in Portugal.

By Ian Allison | Edited by Sheldon Reback Updated Oct 28, 2026, 6:21 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 5:00 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo (CoinDesk) Summary Show Tokenization platform Securitize added Stellar to the list of blockchains it supports, which includes Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche. Securitize said Stellar is known for being a fast and scalable blockchain, where decentralized assets can be configured for know-your-customer, clawbacks and sanctions compliance. Franklin Templeton runs a tokenized money market fund on Stellar, and MoneyGram moves money across it daily.

Securitize (SECZ), which converts real-world assets such as equity and debt into tokens that can be traded like cryptocurrencies, said it added Stellar to its list of supported blockchains.

The company already works closely with Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche and is known for issuing and managing BlackRock’s BUIDL tokenized money-market fund.

Tokenization, the process of bringing assets onto a blockchain, has been generating headlines in recent months, with a growing number of companies saying they’re offering, or planning to offer, versions of shares , bonds and commodities that can be traded around the clock with few, if any, geographic restrictions.

Stellar is known for being a fast and scalable blockchain, where decentralized assets can be configured for customer identification (KYC), clawbacks and sanctions compliance, the firms said at Meridian 2026, the Stellar Development Foundation’s annual conference in Lisbon. Franklin Templeton runs a tokenized money market fund on Stellar, and MoneyGram moves money across it daily.

“The Stellar network has built the fourth-largest ecosystem for tokenized real-world assets, which speaks to the strength of its network and the growing institutional demand for tokenization,” said Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo in a statement.

Securitize, founded in 2017, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in July, putting its own stock on Solana (SOL) and Avalanche (AVAX) at the same time. The shares, which rose as high as $13.70 on the first day of trading, closed at $8.16 on Tuesday.

Disclaimer: Stellar paid for the reporter’s trip to Portugal to cover the conference.

CORRECT (Oct. 28, 10:20 UTC): Corrects company name in final paragraph, an earlier version of the story said Stellar went public. Adds Tuesday’s closing share price.

By Ian Allison | Edited by Sheldon Reback Updated Oct 28, 2026, 6:21 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 5:00 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo (CoinDesk) Summary Show Tokenization platform Securitize added Stellar to the list of blockchains it supports, which includes Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche. Securitize said Stellar is known for being a fast and scalable blockchain, where decentralized assets can be configured for know-your-customer, clawbacks and sanctions compliance. Franklin Templeton runs a tokenized money market fund on Stellar, and MoneyGram moves money across it daily.

Securitize (SECZ), which converts real-world assets such as equity and debt into tokens that can be traded like cryptocurrencies, said it added Stellar to its list of supported blockchains.

The company already works closely with Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche and is known for issuing and managing BlackRock’s BUIDL tokenized money-market fund.

Tokenization, the process of bringing assets onto a blockchain, has been generating headlines in recent months, with a growing number of companies saying they’re offering, or planning to offer, versions of shares , bonds and commodities that can be traded around the clock with few, if any, geographic restrictions.

Stellar is known for being a fast and scalable blockchain, where decentralized assets can be configured for customer identification (KYC), clawbacks and sanctions compliance, the firms said at Meridian 2026, the Stellar Development Foundation’s annual conference in Lisbon. Franklin Templeton runs a tokenized money market fund on Stellar, and MoneyGram moves money across it daily.

“The Stellar network has built the fourth-largest ecosystem for tokenized real-world assets, which speaks to the strength of its network and the growing institutional demand for tokenization,” said Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo in a statement.

Securitize, founded in 2017, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in July, putting its own stock on Solana (SOL) and Avalanche (AVAX) at the same time. The shares, which rose as high as $13.70 on the first day of trading, closed at $8.16 on Tuesday.

posts.title: Outpoll Trading: Bridging Crypto, Stocks, Indices, and Commodities
posts.titleVi: Outpoll Trading: Bridging Crypto, Stocks, Indices, and Commodities
posts.summary: Trading across different financial markets often means switching between platforms to access cryptocurrencies, stocks, indices, and commodities.
posts.summaryVi: Trading across different financial markets often means switching between platforms to access cryptocurrencies, stocks, indices, and commodities.
posts.content:
Trading across different financial markets often means switching between platforms to access cryptocurrencies, stocks, indices, and commodities. Although some platforms offer access to multiple asset classes, traders sometimes find themselves managing different accounts and moving between different interfaces to trade their preferred markets.

Having access to these markets from a single platform can make the process more convenient. This is exactly what Outpoll aims to achieve with its Trading interface. The platform allows users to trade 100+ perpetual markets covering crypto assets and traditional financial assets, with high leverage.

This article takes a closer look at Outpoll Trading, how it works, its key features, and how users can get started.

Outpoll Trading is a perpetual futures trading platform that lets users speculate on the price of an asset without owning it or worrying about an expiration date. Traders can go long or short on crypto, stocks, indices, and commodities with leverage of up to 100x.

As mentioned earlier, Outpoll Trading aims to address the fragmentation issue that has persisted in the world of finance, where traders may need to use different platforms to access their preferred markets. This means spending more time and effort managing multiple accounts, funding them, and familiarizing themselves with different trading interfaces.

Outpoll Trading addresses this by bringing these asset groups together on a single platform through its mobile app. This allows traders to take positions across different markets without having to switch between platforms.

Outpoll Trading’s crypto section supports over 80 assets, such as Bitcoin (BTC), Solana (SOL), Ripple (XRP), Hyperliquid (HYPE), and Dogecoin (DOGE). The platform also features over 20 stocks and indices, including Apple (AAPL), Nvidia (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), and SPX500. There are also four commodities, including oil (OIL), gold (XAU), and natural gas (NG).

These assets are quoted against USDC and USDT. In other words, traders can deposit and lock up either of these stablecoins in their trading accounts to back their leveraged positions. The best part? This applies regardless of the asset group one is trading. So users don’t need to own actual Tesla shares or physical gold bars to trade contracts based on their prices.

Another advantage of using these stablecoins is that users can easily track their profits or losses, since they are calculated and settled in USDC or USDT. At the time of writing this review, more assets are quoted against USDT than USDC.

Outpoll is available in eight languages, including English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese.

Outpoll Trading offers a lineup of features that make it appealing to traders. They include:

Probably Outpoll Trading’s most prominent feature is its perpetual futures trading. Unlike conventional futures trading, where contracts have an expiration date, perp trading lets traders keep a position open without an expiration date. As long as the user has enough margin to back the trade, they can continue to hold that position.

The platform also offers leverage up to 100x. This determines how dramatically the user’s position can move up or down.

Outpoll Trading offers inverse perpetual trading. This is a type of crypto futures contract with no expiration date, and the contract’s value is quoted in USD. Here’s the catch: Margin, collateral, and profit/loss (PnL) are settled in the crypto itself, not the quoted currency.

For example, if a trader holds a BTCUSD inverse perp contract, it means their BTC will be the margin. Because BTC is volatile, the trader’s margin will constantly change along with the asset’s price.Inverse perpetual trading is best for traders who are actively accumulating crypto and expecting value to increase over time. The idea behind this approach is that as the collateral value rises, the trader’s profit increases when prices pick up.

Outpoll Trading offers inverse perpetual trading for four crypto assets. They are BTCUSD, ETHUSD, SOLUSD, and LTCUSD.

Outpoll Trading sets a high bar by enabling access to a wide variety of asset groups. As mentioned earlier, these groups are crypto (BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL, ZEC, etc.), stocks (MSTR, TSLA, NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, etc.), indices (SPX500), and commodities (OIL, XAU, NG).

On Outpoll Trading’s interface, these digital assets are grouped as either crypto or real-world assets (RWAs). For context, RWAs are physical or TradFi assets that become tradable on the blockchain as digital assets. Outpoll Trading tags real-world assets with an “RWA” tag to distinguish them from their crypto counterparts.

Because these assets are tradable as perpetual futures contracts, it means that traders do not hold the actual digital asset. Instead, they hold a contract representing the asset’s value, allowing them to speculate on its future price.

Like most perp futures trading interfaces, Outpoll offers an easy-to-navigate trading interface. The most prominent features fall into margin modes and order types.

The margin modes comprise cross and isolated margins. Cross margin involves using one’s entire account balance to back open positions. In most cases, experienced traders use this margin. Isolated margin, on the other hand, involves each trading pair having its own independent margin. This is a beginner-friendly option.

The order types include the market order, limit order, and stop order. Traders execute a market order when they buy or sell an asset at the best available current price. A limit order involves buying or selling an asset only at a specific price. A stop order (or stop-loss) lets traders set a price at which an asset will trigger a buy or sell order automatically.

In addition to the web version, Outpoll offers a mobile app available on Android devices. As of this writing, the team has not launched the app for iOS devices. The mobile app offers all the platform’s trading services, making navigation as seamless as possible.

Outpoll Trading boasts a simple, user-friendly interface on both web and mobile. In this review, we will see how to execute a trade on Outpoll Trading using the web version:

Here are the pros and cons of using Outpoll Trading:

Outpoll is a digital platform that made its public debut in June 2026 through its dedicated centralized-decentralized finance (CeDeFi) prediction market. This allowed eligible users to buy or sell contracts tied to the outcome of future events. The debut also included a mobile app for Android users.

While Outpoll originally started as a prediction market, on October 15, 2026, it debuted its Trading platform. According to the announcement, the Trading interface was designed to operate side by side with the prediction markets interface. “Prediction markets show what people expect. Futures let you act on what the price does,” the platform stated.

Traders are constantly looking for easier ways to access their preferred financial markets. Little wonder financial platforms continue to make their interfaces as intuitive as possible. Outpoll takes a similar approach by bringing crypto, stocks, indices, and commodities together under one trading interface.

The platform allows traders to access over 100 perpetual futures markets without having to switch between different trading apps. With its prediction markets and Trading interfaces operating side by side, users can also access both products through a single account.

Admittedly, perpetual futures trading can net significant gains for some traders. Still, it is worth noting that trading these contracts on Outpoll Trading carries substantial risks, particularly when leverage is involved. While leverage can amplify potential profits, it can also increase losses and lead to liquidation. Therefore, users should understand these risks before trading.

Another thing worth bearing in mind is Outpoll’s geographical reach. During sign-up, Outpoll requires users to confirm that they do not reside in restricted jurisdictions before completing the account creation process. These include the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, and Singapore. At the time of writing, users in these regions are restricted from accessing the platform.

Bridgit Murphy is a blockchain technology engineer specializing in integrated online services, smart contracts, fork development, and quality assurance. An open-source enthusiast, Murphy recently relocated from her hometown of Dublin to Hong Kong.

posts.content:
Robinhood links 29 million app users to Ripple’s XRP Ledger

RLUSD already trades on Bitstamp, while the new agreement adds expected Robinhood app access and planned XRP Ledger settlement.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Robinhood expects RLUSD in its app later in 2026 under its Ripple agreement, with eligible jurisdictions still undisclosed. 02 Bitstamp announced RLUSD trading on Ethereum in January 2025, so the new agreement expands an existing exchange relationship. 03 Planned XRP Ledger settlement and treasury integration extend the partnership, but the announcement gives no institutional settlement start date. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Robinhood expects to add Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin to its app later in 2026 under an agreement announced Oct. 27 that also includes plans for institutional settlement on the XRP Ledger.

The planned app rollout would give customers another way to access RLUSD, though the announcement specifies neither a launch date nor which countries or states will be eligible. Those details will determine which Robinhood customers can use the token.

The agreement expands a relationship with an established trading venue. Ripple said RLUSD was already live on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp by Robinhood when it announced the partnership.

From exchange access to institutional settlement

Bitstamp announced its RLUSD listing on Jan. 8, 2025 , using the Ethereum network . Its notice listed trading pairs against the euro, US dollar, USDT, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP, while excluding the EU and warning that not every pair was available in every jurisdiction.

The October agreement builds on that exchange access with a planned Robinhood app rollout and a separate institutional settlement use.

Bitstamp’s listing notice described backing by cash and cash equivalents and support for RLUSD on both Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, while specifying that its own listing then used Ethereum.

Bitstamp’s historical Ethereum trading and the planned XRP Ledger settlement service have separate timelines. The January 2025 EU exclusion also provides no eligibility answer for Robinhood’s future app rollout.

Related Reading Ripple targets trillion-dollar securities markets with new US brokerage and South Korean deals

Robinhood plans to use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for institutional settlement of transactions between financial firms across Bitstamp’s institutional business. Ripple’s announcement does not say when the service will begin or how much it will settle, leaving the intended scale unresolved.

Bitstamp already lists RLUSD on Ethereum, while Robinhood app access and XRPL institutional settlement remain planned. Robinhood also plans to integrate Ripple Treasury for its own cash and liquidity management, forecasting, payments, risk management, and intercompany netting, which offsets amounts owed between parts of the company.

That addresses the company’s financial operations, a separate part of the agreement from customer access to RLUSD.

Ripple Prime provides Bitstamp with lending and margin financing across roughly 20 digital assets and gives Prime clients access to Bitstamp spot trading. Prime support for Bitstamp perpetual futures is planned for later in 2026.

For Robinhood app customers, the next milestone is a launch notice specifying eligibility and supported RLUSD functions. For institutions, a settlement start date and reported activity would show how far the agreement has moved into operation.

Bitcoin ETF inflows climb to $176M as BTC rebounds above $80K

Markets Published Oct 28, 2026 US spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $286 million over two days, narrowing October’s net outflows to $26 million as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index remained neutral.

US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted about $176 million in net inflows on Tuesday, extending their recovery to a second consecutive trading day.

The inflows rose from $110 million on Monday , bringing the two-day total to $286 million, according to SoSoValue data.

The rebound followed nearly $774 million in withdrawals on Thursday and Friday . October net outflows narrowed to about $26 million through Tuesday, while year-to-date net inflows stood at roughly $850 million.

Market sentiment also edged higher. Alternative.me’s Crypto Fear & Greed Index rose to 51 from 48 the previous day, remaining in “Neutral” territory. The reading was still below 63, or “Greed,” a week earlier.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded at about $80,818 at the time of publication, up 1.6% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

Meanwhile, US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs continued to see withdrawals , recording about $149 million in net outflows on Monday and Tuesday after four straight weeks of net outflows.

Their October net outflows reached $1.32 billion through Tuesday, putting the month on track for the largest net withdrawals since November 2025.

Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Coinbase denies systems breach, says vendor exposed customer data

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 Coinbase said that an incident at analytics vendor Amplitude exposed some customers’ contact data, but it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its own systems.

Some Coinbase customers’ contact information was exposed in a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude, the exchange said Wednesday.

The incident impacted a “small subset” of Coinbase customers, along with other Amplitude clients, Coinbase Support said on X.

Coinbase denied that its own systems had been breached and said customer funds were not affected.

The disclosure adds to Wednesday’s reports of cyberattacks affecting both crypto exchanges and traditional financial firms. In South Korea, Bithumb is investigating whether a breach of its internal work platform exposed customer information, while brokerage Daishin Securities reported a leak of personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers.

Cointelegraph contacted Coinbase to find out how many customers were affected but had not received a response by publication.

In May 2025, Coinbase disclosed a separate data breach that impacted less than 1% of its monthly transacting users. The exchange estimated reimbursement and remediation costs at up to $400 million .

posts.title: Ripple Price Analysis: XRP Must Reclaim This Key Level to Restart the Rally
posts.titleVi: Ripple Price Analysis: XRP Must Reclaim This Key Level to Restart the Rally
posts.summary: XRP is rebounding toward $1.32 after defending the $1.26 support for the second time in October. The asset now pushes toward a short-term descending channel’s upper boundary and the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement.
posts.summaryVi: XRP is rebounding toward $1.32 after defending the $1.26 support for the second time in October. The asset now pushes toward a short-term descending channel’s upper boundary and the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement.
posts.content:
XRP is rebounding toward $1.32 after defending the $1.26 support for the second time in October. The asset now pushes toward a short-term descending channel’s upper boundary and the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement. A breakout from this area could shift the short-term structure, while another rejection would keep sellers in control.

On the daily chart, XRP is correcting the August rally from $0.99 to the $1.70 high. The decline has carried the price below the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement at $1.34, which now acts as resistance. The failed attempt to break back above $1.40 on October 21 reinforced the bearish short-term structure.

The key support is $1.26, where the 0.618 retracement overlaps with a prior demand zone. Two lower wicks into this area suggest buyers are responding, but the rebounds have remained modest. For now, the level continues to hold, yet the market has not confirmed a reversal.

On the upside, a reclaim of $1.34 would be the first sign of improvement, opening the way toward the $1.40 supply zone. Beyond that, the $1.50 region marks the origin of the last major breakdown and the next significant overhead barrier.

Conversely, if $1.26 breaks on a decisive daily close, XRP could slide toward the 0.702 retracement at $1.20. Below that, $1.14 stands out as the 0.786 retracement and the top of the demand block that launched the August rally.

The 4-hour chart shows XRP trading inside a descending channel since the late-September high near $1.65, with consistent lower highs. The upper boundary rejected the price near $1.40 on October 21, triggering a sharp decline back toward the $1.26 demand zone. That reaction confirmed the trendline as dynamic resistance.

Buyers have since defended the $1.26 area twice, producing a series of slightly higher lows. XRP is now climbing toward the channel’s upper boundary around $1.34, which overlaps with the daily 0.5 retracement. This confluence makes the next few candles important for the short-term direction.

A decisive breakout above the trendline could trigger a relief rally toward the $1.40 supply zone. Clearing it would weaken the bearish channel and bring $1.50 back into focus. Failing that, a rejection near $1.34 would likely send the price back to retest support.

A 4-hour close below $1.26, together with a loss of the channel’s lower boundary near $1.23, would suggest buyers are losing control. In that scenario, the $1.20 level would likely be the next downside target. The channel therefore remains the dominant pattern. Until XRP breaks above its upper boundary, rebounds toward $1.34 are more likely to face selling pressure than to confirm a trend reversal.

posts.title: Bithumb Users Face Phishing Risks After Reported Data Leak
posts.titleVi: Bithumb Users Face Phishing Risks After Reported Data Leak
posts.summary: Some customer personal data at South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, Bithumb, was reportedly leaked on October 28 after an external unauthorized party accessed one of its internal workplace tools.
posts.summaryVi: Some customer personal data at South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, Bithumb, was reportedly leaked on October 28 after an external unauthorized party accessed one of its internal workplace tools.
posts.content:
Some customer personal data at South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, Bithumb, was reportedly leaked on October 28 after an external unauthorized party accessed one of its internal workplace tools.

This is the latest in a string of similar incidents that have cut across crypto companies and traditional financial firms.

According to the Yonhap News Agency, the exchange detected abnormal access by an outsider without authority on October 27, inside its in-house mobile groupware system.

While the exchange is said to still be working out the exact scope of the breach, another firm, Daishin Securities, which was also hit, reported that information on more than 38,000 of its customers, including names, emails, and phone numbers, was leaked.

Mirae Asset Global Investment was also a victim, and Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) is said to be investigating all three incidents and has already sent an on-site team to Daishin. At a meeting with the chairmen of eight bank holding companies, FSS Director Lee Chan-jin pressed the financial sector on IT security, saying:

“As artificial intelligence is used as a means of hacking, security vulnerabilities will be easily detected and simultaneous attacks will become a regular occurrence.”

He added that boards must now take the lead in improving the security capabilities of their companies.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) also reacted to the news, telling his 12.9 million followers on X that while they may not be able to prevent leaks, they could take measures to protect themselves, including reducing the information they share and locking down their accounts. Leaked exchange data, he pointed out, mostly feeds phishing and SIM-swapping attacks, and he recommended using a unique email alias for each exchange and hardware keys or passkeys instead of SMS codes.

“Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, ‘security issues,’ or ‘refund recovery’ is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades,” CZ cautioned.

The Bithumb case has come right in the middle of other security disclosures involving crypto businesses, with hardware wallet maker Foundation saying yesterday that its customers had been hit with more than 23,000 phishing emails sent from its official domain after hackers compromised its API keys on Cloudflare.

Recall that in August, a Trezor provider named ShipMonk had the names, locations, and emails of more than 67,000 users stolen , while more recently, Keystone Wallet, another major provider, reported that unauthorized people accessed its official website and stole the shipping information of its customers, although they did not compromise wallet passwords and private keys.

There was also an incident today involving Amplitude, a Coinbase vendor, where a subset of the exchange’s users reportedly had their contact details exposed, with SlowMist claiming that the hacker had gotten the details of more than 70,000 customers. However, Coinbase support rejected the breach label, stating that it had not seen any evidence of unauthorized people accessing its systems. It also told users that their funds were unaffected.

posts.title: Binance Alerts Users: Ethereum Deposits Paused and Major Delistings Ahead
posts.titleVi: Binance Alerts Users: Ethereum Deposits Paused and Major Delistings Ahead
posts.summary: The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange will briefly suspend some important services on the Ethereum (ETH) network this week. It will also remove several trading pairs that no longer meet the required standards. Here’s everything users should know.
posts.summaryVi: The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange will briefly suspend some important services on the Ethereum (ETH) network this week. It will also remove several trading pairs that no longer meet the required standards. Here’s everything users should know.
posts.content:
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange will briefly suspend some important services on the Ethereum (ETH) network this week.

It will also remove several trading pairs that no longer meet the required standards. Here’s everything users should know.

Binance will perform wallet maintenance on the ETH network on October 28, and deposits and withdrawals on that blockchain will be temporarily unavailable during the process. The effort is scheduled to take about one hour, after which operations will resume.

As usual, the company assured that token trading on the network will not be affected and promised to handle all user-related technical requirements.

“Deposits and withdrawals for token(s) on the aforementioned network will be reopened once the upgraded network is deemed to be stable. No further announcement will be posted,” the announcement reads.

Binance has performed many similar wallet maintenance events this year, with no reports of issues or user complaints. In August, it temporarily paused transfers on the Ethereum network, while prior to that, it briefly suspended TRX deposits and withdrawals.

Besides the update regarding the Ethereum network, Binance revealed that it will delist the following spot trading pairs: AAVE/BTC, ATOM/BTC, CAKE/BTC, DASH/BTC, ETC/BTC, ICP/BTC, PENDLE/BTC, RENDER/BTC, TAO/BTC, THETA/BTC, XAUT/BTC and XTZ/BTC on October 30.

The decision follows a rigorous check of all listed pairs on the platform, as the exchange regularly checks whether they meet certain standards such as adequate liquidity and trading volume.

“The delisting of a spot trading pair does not affect the availability of the tokens on Binance Spot. Users can still trade the spot trading pair’s base and quote assets on other trading pair(s) that are available on Binance,” the entity explained.

In addition, Binance will say goodbye to ten margin trading pairs on the same date. Those in question include RE/USD1, 币安人生/U, KAT/U, BTC/USDS, ETH/USDS, AVNT/U, FET/U, TRUMP/U, APT/U, WLFI/U.

The announced delistings haven’t triggered major price moves for the involved cryptocurrencies. This is hardly surprising, as stronger market reactions typically occur when Binance discontinues all services for a given digital asset.

That was the case earlier this month, when the exchange removed Epic Chain (EPIC) and QuickSwap (QUICK), triggering severe crashes in both.

Dimitar got interested in cryptocurrencies back in 2018 amid the prolonged bear market. His biggest passion in the field is Bitcoin and he was fascinated with its journey. With a flair for producing high-quality content, he started covering the cryptocurrency space in late 2018. His hobby is football.

Besides the update regarding the Ethereum network, Binance revealed that it will delist the following spot trading pairs: AAVE/BTC, ATOM/BTC, CAKE/BTC, DASH/BTC, ETC/BTC, ICP/BTC, PENDLE/BTC, RENDER/BTC, TAO/BTC, THETA/BTC, XAUT/BTC and XTZ/BTC on October 30.

The decision follows a rigorous check of all listed pairs on the platform, as the exchange regularly checks whether they meet certain standards such as adequate liquidity and trading volume.

“The delisting of a spot trading pair does not affect the availability of the tokens on Binance Spot. Users can still trade the spot trading pair’s base and quote assets on other trading pair(s) that are available on Binance,” the entity explained.

In addition, Binance will say goodbye to ten margin trading pairs on the same date. Those in question include RE/USD1, 币安人生/U, KAT/U, BTC/USDS, ETH/USDS, AVNT/U, FET/U, TRUMP/U, APT/U, WLFI/U.

The announced delistings haven’t triggered major price moves for the involved cryptocurrencies. This is hardly surprising, as stronger market reactions typically occur when Binance discontinues all services for a given digital asset.

That was the case earlier this month, when the exchange removed Epic Chain (EPIC) and QuickSwap (QUICK), triggering severe crashes in both.

Bitcoin apps risk massive fee drain, and 2 library bugs are blamed

Two Bitcoin library flaws could hide massive miner fees and let valid transactions bypass safety checks.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Bitcoinjs-lib's Oct. 26 advisories identify fee-accounting fixes in versions 5.2.2, 6.1.9 and 7.0.4 for the corresponding release lines. 02 Conflicting or missing input-value records can understate miner fees and defeat safeguards when applications trust the vulnerable library's accounting. 03 Actual loss requires an authorized, valid transaction to be broadcast and accepted; maintainers should upgrade or independently verify input values. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoinjs-lib, a library used to build Bitcoin applications, has patched two bugs that can make software understate the miner fee a valid transaction would pay if broadcast and accepted.

The Oct. 26 security disclosures identify fixes in versions 5.2.2, 6.1.9 and 7.0.4 for the corresponding release lines.

The affected format is a partially signed Bitcoin transaction (PSBT), and BIP 174 defines it as a way to pass transaction information and signatures between clients. Signing, combining signatures, finalizing inputs, and extracting the transaction are separate functions, even when one application performs several of them.

The risk concerns applications that import these packages and trust bitcoinjs-lib's fee calculation or excessive-fee safeguard without independently checking the outputs being spent. Maintainers need to review their dependency version and how they validate imported PSBTs.

Why valid signatures can accompany misleading fees

A Bitcoin transaction's fee is the difference between the value of its inputs and its outputs, so understating an input makes the calculated fee look smaller.

In the first flaw, signing and fee accounting can use different values for the same input. Signing uses the full previous transaction, while fee accounting prefers a conflicting record containing a smaller value. As a result, the vulnerable software can authorize the real transaction while evaluating the wrong fee.

The advisory describes a demonstration on bitcoinjs-lib 7.0.1 in which the actual fee was 900,000,000 satoshi, but the library reported 200 satoshi. The signature verified, and extraction returned without the default fee-rate warning.

Related Reading Eclair merges fixes for Lightning flaws that could burn Bitcoin in fees

The second advisory describes finalized inputs with both input-value records missing. The calculator counts those inputs as zero, and an already-signed PSBT imported from another party can reach this calculation without needing another signing operation.

Its hypothetical example has a true fee of 91,000 satoshi but a reported fee of 1,000 satoshi. Finalized scripts and signatures alone do not establish the missing input's value.

A bitcoinjs-lib flaw could count missing PSBT input values as zero, hiding a much larger fee; patched releases now require every value. Actual loss requires an authorized, valid transaction to be broadcast and accepted by the network. These defects do not create signatures, and excess value becomes a miner fee.

For conflicting records, affected releases are 5.2.0 through 5.2.1, 6.0.0 through 6.1.8 including 6.1.0-rc.0, and 7.0.0-rc.0 through 7.0.3. The missing-record flaw affects the same v6 and v7 ranges, plus 5.1.0 through 5.2.1 in the v5 line.

The remediation gives signing and accounting a shared method for resolving previous outputs, rejects conflicting values or scripts, and requires an amount for every input during fee calculation. It also clears cached fees and extracted transactions after relevant metadata changes or combinations.

Maintainers unable to upgrade should independently verify referenced output values. Reject conflicting records before signing or trusting fees, and verify every input value before trusting fees or extracting a transaction.

Markets Bitcoin treasury Datavault AI plunges 50% after firm says it can’t access its BTC

The company said the accounting correction will cut reported assets by $92.2 million at the end of 2025 after bitcoin held on Biconomy could not be withdrawn.

By Shaurya Malwa Updated Oct 28, 2026, 7:34 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 1:28 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Bitcoin treasury Datavault AI plunges 50% after firm says it can’t access its BTC. (Meg Boulden/Unsplash) Summary Show Datavault AI shares plunged nearly 50 percent Tuesday after the company disclosed that it had been unable to withdraw bitcoin from the Biconomy exchange since June and would restate its financial results. The company said bitcoin credited through Scilex Holding Company’s $150 million investment should have been recorded as an amount owed by Scilex, reducing reported assets by $92.2 million at the end of 2025 and $49 million as of June 2026. Datavault had treated the bitcoin as funding available to sustain operations, but the unresolved withdrawal now requires the company to reassess that assumption.

Datavault AI (DVLT) shares plunged nearly 50% on Tuesday after a filing revealed that the company had been unable to withdraw bitcoin from crypto exchange Biconomy since June and would have to restate its financial results.

Stocks of the Oregon, U.S.-based company closed at $0.067, down 49.55%, with roughly 244 million shares traded.

The problem traces back to a September 2025 agreement with Scilex Holding Company, which agreed to purchase $150 million of Datavault shares and warrants using bitcoin.

Scilex credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault’s account at Biconomy through off-chain transfers, meaning the balances changed within the exchange rather than through transactions on Bitcoin’s blockchain. Datavault subsequently sold 491.4 BTC back to Scilex for about $40.5 million in cash.

But the transfer could not be completed when it requested a withdrawal to an external account in June, the company said, and remained incomplete as of Monday’s filing.

Biconomy was also involved in supplying the bitcoin behind the investment. Scilex’s June financial report says it sold $200 million of shares in its subsidiary Semnur to Biconomy for bitcoin, then used $150 million to buy Datavault securities.

Datavault now says the bitcoin credited through Scilex’s investment should have been recorded as an amount Scilex owed for the shares. That amount would reduce shareholders’ equity instead of appearing among Datavault’s cryptocurrency assets.

The correction is expected to reduce reported assets by $92.2 million at the end of 2025 and $49 million as of June 2026. Datavault had counted those bitcoin balances as money it could draw on to keep the business running, but must now revisit the assessment.

CoinDesk contacted Biconomy about the withdrawal request and the bitcoin backing Datavault’s account and did not receive a response as of Asian afternoon hours Wednesday.

The breach hit an internal employee system that Bithumb says is separate from its trading platform, while the exchange is still determining whether customer information was exposed.

By Shaurya Malwa Oct 28, 2026, 1:10 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Bithumb hacked through employee system as South Korean financial firms face cyberattacks. (Bithumb) Summary Show Bithumb said an outsider breached an internal employee mobile system and stole personal information, but no cryptocurrency funds were reported lost. The South Korean exchange said the compromised system was separate from its trading platform, though it has not disclosed how many people were affected or whether deposits and withdrawals were disrupted. The breach comes amid cyberattacks on South Korean financial firms and follows Bithumb’s erroneous $40 billion Bitcoin credit to customers in February.

Bithumb, South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, said earlier Wednesday an outsider broke into the internal mobile system its employees use to work and message each other and that personal information was taken.

No crypto funds were reported lost as of Asian afternoon hours. Bithumb is the second-largest exchange in South Korea by trading volumes.

The exchange found the intrusion on Tuesday and reported to the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission, according to Korean media. It told Yonhap it was analyzing the exact scope, “including the possibility of member information being involved.”

It said the breached system runs separately from its trading platform, so “customer virtual assets cannot be accessed through this breach.” It has not said whether deposits or withdrawals were affected or how many people’s data was exposed.

Bithumb was one of three financial firms the Financial Supervisory Service said it was assessing on Wednesday. Daishin Securities said personal and credit information for 38,490 of its customers leaked in an outside attack. Mirae Asset Global Investments said it blocked abnormal access to some of its web systems and that investor information was not affected.

“I understand that major financial investment companies experienced overall hacking incidents yesterday,” FSS Governor Lee Chan-jin told a meeting with bank holding company chairs. Earlier in the month he said cyberattacks had hit 16 South Korean financial firms as of Oct. 14.

Meanwhile, this is a second hit to Bithumb’s controls this year.

In February it mistakenly credited customers with 620,000 BTC, worth more than $40 billion at the time, instead of 620,000 won. CEO Lee Jae-won blamed the error on weak internal controls at the time, saying the exchange was “acutely aware of the deficiency in internal system control.”

posts.title: XRP Whales Now Control 68.5% of Supply, Highest Level Since 2022
posts.titleVi: XRP Whales Now Control 68.5% of Supply, Highest Level Since 2022
posts.summary: XRP whales have held the largest share of the token’s supply since November 2022. Wallets holding at least 10 million XRP now control 46.87 billion tokens, or around 68.5% of the total supply. The increase comes as the price struggles near $1.3.
posts.summaryVi: XRP whales have held the largest share of the token’s supply since November 2022. Wallets holding at least 10 million XRP now control 46.87 billion tokens, or around 68.5% of the total supply. The increase comes as the price struggles near $1.3.
posts.content:
XRP whales have held the largest share of the token’s supply since November 2022. Wallets holding at least 10 million XRP now control 46.87 billion tokens, or around 68.5% of the total supply.

The increase comes as the price struggles near $1.3. According to Santiment, this shows that large holders continue to accumulate despite the current weakness.

The latest trend suggests major investors are maintaining their exposure while smaller traders may be losing confidence. But Santiment explained that the crypto asset still needs to clear important levels before a stronger recovery can take shape. The $1.3 mark remains a crucial level, while $1.5 could offer stronger confirmation of bullish momentum. Holding above $1.2, alongside continued whale accumulation, would support the outlook.

Further gains in whale holdings could strengthen the recovery case.

Meanwhile, XRP exchange outflows reached around 5.3 billion tokens over a 30-day period. The figure remains below the 6 billion XRP recorded in October. With approximately 2.206 billion tokens leaving, Binance accounted for the largest share. Next up was OKX with 501.51 million, followed by Bybit, which recorded 479.94 million in outflows. Upbit saw around 392.90 million XRP leave its platform, followed by Bitget at 243.39 million.

The outflows declined during the first half of August before picking up later that month. Higher levels continued through September and October, in a recovery from the quieter summer period. These movements may mean more XRP is moving into private wallets or other platforms. That could reduce the tokens readily available for sale on exchanges.

Additionally, the TD Sequential indicator has flashed a buy signal on the three-day chart. The last three similar signals were followed by rebounds of 31%, 24%, and 18%.

On the ETF front, however, US-listed spot XRP funds started the week with $3.61 million in outflows, reversing course after ending the previous week in positive territory.

On the corporate investment side of things, Evernorth Holdings is looking to raise up to $80.7 million through an equity facility with Cantor Fitzgerald. It plans to use part of the proceeds to buy more XRP, while also funding its operations and developing products across the XRP ecosystem.

The move comes as the company builds on its recently launched Nasdaq listing under the ticker XRPN. Evernorth already holds around 473 million XRP in its treasury and aims to generate returns through institutional strategies. It has also partnered with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and BitGo to support those plans.

Additionally, Ripple is expanding its corporate treasury platform with AI-powered automation and round-the-clock payment services. Its new 24/7 Returns feature could allow eligible businesses to earn returns on qualifying digital assets, including RLUSD, beyond traditional banking hours.

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says tokenized equities need more than a temporary SEC exemption to flourish in the US.

Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says uncertainty over the longevity of US tokenization rules could prevent investors from committing substantial assets to tokenized markets, despite the securities regulator opening a temporary path for onchain stock trading this year.

Speaking during Robinhood’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Tenev welcomed the SEC’s innovation exemption but said further rulemaking or legislation would be needed to provide longer-term regulatory certainty.

“As far as the innovation exemption goes, I think it’s a really positive step... I do think more needs to be done to give people a little bit of certainty because as we talk to customers, I think the uncertainty of what happens in five years is likely to be an impediment to, like, putting serious assets onto this technology.”

Tokenized stock offerings have faced resistance from traditional issuers. Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs were among 16 companies that objected to their shares being offered on the proposed OKXICE venue, while AMC CEO Adam Aron separately criticized Robinhood’s tokenized stock products.

Despite the regulatory uncertainty, Binance Research projects that the tokenized equities market could grow to $349 billion by 2030 under its base-case scenario, from $4.43 billion as of Sept. 15.

Related: SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinations

“So I still think some rule-making or legislation is going to be necessary, even though, of course, it’s a positive step, and we hope to have more to share on our own US tokenization plans in the near future,” said Tenev.

Asked about private-company stock tokens, Tenev said Robinhood intends to launch those products overseas, subject to regulatory arrangements. In the US, Tenev said the company is working to find a path that satisfies current accreditation constraints.

Robinhood offers around 200 stock tokens on Robinhood Chain . The products are backed by underlying shares but structured as tokenized debt securities, providing economic exposure without the same shareholder rights as conventional stocks.

That distinction leaves their current structure outside the SEC’s innovation exemption, which requires equivalent rights, including dividends and voting rights.

Tenev’s comments came as Robinhood reported a 55% year-on-year fall in cryptocurrency revenue to $120 million in the third quarter, while crypto notional trading volume declined 38% to $50 billion.

Trading volume on the Robinhood app fell 48% to $21 billion, while Bitstamp volume fell 28% to $29 billion.

Robinhood’s prediction market business went in the opposite direction. Event-contract revenue rose sixfold to $173 million, while contracts traded increased more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion.

Across the wider business, total net revenue rose 12% to a record $1.42 billion, below analyst expectations. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.60, missing estimates by 4 cents.

“So I still think some rule-making or legislation is going to be necessary, even though, of course, it’s a positive step, and we hope to have more to share on our own US tokenization plans in the near future,” said Tenev.

Asked about private-company stock tokens, Tenev said Robinhood intends to launch those products overseas, subject to regulatory arrangements. In the US, Tenev said the company is working to find a path that satisfies current accreditation constraints.

Robinhood offers around 200 stock tokens on Robinhood Chain . The products are backed by underlying shares but structured as tokenized debt securities, providing economic exposure without the same shareholder rights as conventional stocks.

That distinction leaves their current structure outside the SEC’s innovation exemption, which requires equivalent rights, including dividends and voting rights.

Tenev’s comments came as Robinhood reported a 55% year-on-year fall in cryptocurrency revenue to $120 million in the third quarter, while crypto notional trading volume declined 38% to $50 billion.

Trading volume on the Robinhood app fell 48% to $21 billion, while Bitstamp volume fell 28% to $29 billion.

Robinhood’s prediction market business went in the opposite direction. Event-contract revenue rose sixfold to $173 million, while contracts traded increased more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion.

Across the wider business, total net revenue rose 12% to a record $1.42 billion, below analyst expectations. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.60, missing estimates by 4 cents.

BNY offers XRP custody, but only 1 rollout type exists

Eligible clients can now hold XRP through BNY, while transfers of existing tokens would not establish additional purchases.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 BNY now supports XRP and RLUSD custody for eligible institutional clients, adding another route to hold and transfer the tokens. 02 Ripple's announcement discloses no XRP custody balance or new purchase, leaving additional acquisitions as the test of incremental demand. 03 C2FO plans RLUSD settlement on XRPL through a limited rollout, with a waitlist and US-only access at launch. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

BNY now supports custody of XRP and Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin for eligible institutional clients, according to an Oct. 27 announcement from Ripple, giving institutions another way to hold and transfer the XRP Ledger's native token.

The service offers a banking route to safeguard the asset and manage its operations. BNY describes its platform as connecting custody with settlement, accounting and servicing.

The announcement names no funded XRP custody client and discloses neither an XRP balance nor an incremental purchase. Moving tokens that clients already own to BNY would change their custodian without necessarily creating demand for more coins.

BNY’s XRP custody supports transfers and client allocations, but the announcement does not disclose balances or new purchases. What BNY's custody support changes

The change provides a route to custody XRP within BNY's servicing platform. The bank's existing workaround for stablecoins and tokenized assets provides context, but XRP custody directly concerns the token an institution would own.

BNY says its general custody platform uses segregated wallets, operational controls, and oversight. It also presents digital and traditional assets in a combined environment for settlement, accounting and servicing, which can simplify reconciliation and asset administration.

Those functions address how an institution manages an asset after deciding to hold it, and they can reduce operational friction. Yet, custody availability alone does not establish that every institution has the mandate, approvals, or appetite to acquire XRP.

Neither the release nor BNY's platform description provides an XRP-specific list of eligible customers or jurisdictions. BNY says the availability of accounts, products and services varies by customer and location.

Its Oct. 8 European custody expansion was for select institutions. That earlier announcement did not establish XRP-specific availability across the EU, so the bank's geographic presence cannot be treated as a map of where the new XRP service is accessible.

The relationship with Ripple already covered a different layer of digital finance. BNY's selection as RLUSD's primary reserve custodian was announced on July 9, 2025 , involving the reserve assets and cash that support the stablecoin. The Oct. 27 release also cites its custody relationship with Ripple Prime.

The clearest evidence of service use would be XRP deposited into funded client custody accounts. But a balance at BNY would answer only part of the demand question: it would show tokens held there, while leaving open how those tokens were acquired.

Consider an institution that already owns XRP at another custodian. Transferring that position to BNY could increase the bank's reported XRP holdings without any additional market purchase. The same tokens would have a new custody arrangement.

A client acquiring more XRP for a new allocation would be a different development. Connecting custody growth to that kind of acquisition would show the service accompanying additional buying. Establishing that BNY's new access caused the purchase would require a further link to the client's investment decision.

Even growth in a dollar-denominated custody total would need care. A higher token price can lift the value of assets held without increasing the number of XRP. Token balances and evidence of new acquisitions would be more informative together than a custody valuation alone.

Client custody support also provides no basis for treating BNY as an XRP buyer for its own balance sheet. A bank providing safekeeping and a client deciding to acquire tokens are separate participants and decisions.

C2FO, a working-capital platform that helps businesses obtain early payment on approved invoices, announced a separate initiative with Ripple on Oct. 27 . The companies plan to bring financing and settlement supporting C2FO Instant Pay onto the XRP Ledger, using RLUSD for settlement.

The initiative aims to shorten the settlement delay after early payment is arranged, and the relevant follow-up is how much XRP the service would need to operate when its settlement asset is RLUSD.

C2FO's historical working-capital activity describes existing early-payment programs, rather than verified Instant Pay volume settled on XRPL.

The Instant Pay product page sets out the rollout limits: businesses can join a waitlist, access will expand through a limited rollout over the coming months, and the offering will be available only in the US at launch.

The rollout qualifications leave actual uptake and settlement volumes as developments still to observe.

Ripple and BNY say they are examining a C2FO supply-chain financing initiative intended to broaden investor access to approved receivables, subject to client requirements.

They also intend to expand support for XRPL-issued assets and work toward direct RLUSD minting and redemption for BNY clients.

These plans do not establish that invoice principal will be purchased or held in XRP, or that the proposed BNY minting, redemption and financing services have begun.

The ledger's transaction-cost documentation lists a current minimum of 10 drops for a standard transaction, potentially rising under load, with the fee destroyed. Its reserve documentation lists a 1 XRP base reserve and generally 0.2 XRP per qualifying owned ledger item, with exceptions.

Those requirements do not rise dollar for dollar with the principal of an invoice settled in RLUSD. Any larger XRP liquidity or inventory requirement tied to C2FO would need separate evidence about how the service actually operates.

Funded XRP balances and evidence of clients' additional acquisitions would show how institutions use BNY's newly available custody.

C2FO's rollout and settlement activity would answer a separate question about ledger use. For XRP holders, each would be more informative than treating the availability of a service as a measure of token buying.

Bithumb discloses data leak after internal system breach: Report

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 The breach impacted its in-house mobile system, used by employees for work and information sharing.

South Korea’s crypto exchange Bithumb is investigating the extent of a data leak caused by a hack of its internal mobile system earlier this week, Yonhap News Agency reported Wednesday.

Bithumb discovered the breach of its in-house mobile system — the platform used by employees to communicate internally — on Tuesday and notified the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission that day, according to Yonhap , which cited industry sources.

The exchange is investigating the scope of the attack, including whether member data was leaked.

“We are analyzing the exact scope, including the possibility of member information being involved,” Bithumb told Yonhap. “We will provide an official announcement this morning. However, the internal work system is separated from the virtual asset trading system, so customer virtual assets cannot be accessed through this breach.”

Cointelegraph reached out to Bithumb for further comment.

The incident adds to a recent wave of cyberattacks in Korea’s financial sector.

During a meeting at the Financial Supervisory Authority headquarters on Wednesday, Governor Lee Chan-jin said cyberattacks had hit 16 South Korean financial firms as of Oct. 14.

The Korea Times reports that asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities were also recent victims of cyberattacks.

Daishin Securities said that personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers had been leaked. Mirae Asset Global Investments said it had blocked abnormal external access to some web systems and was investigating the incident. The company said investor information was not affected, according to Yonhap.

posts.content:
X100 governance flaws trigger $6M loss due to a flash loan

X100’s attacker repaid a flash loan from theft proceeds while its stake stayed locked, and Arkadiko’s ballot accepted late token purchases.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 X100’s attacker gained two Senate seats and repaid its flash loan while the purchased stake remained locked for a year. 02 Arkadiko’s roughly five-day ballot admitted late token purchases, then activated a malicious contract without a separate execution delay. 03 Arkadiko restored its legitimate contract entry on Oct. 27, but that change alone does not establish recovered collateral or compensation. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

An attacker still acquired two governance seats on X100, a token project with a Senate-governed treasury, and approved a treasury transaction and repaid a flash loan in a single blockchain transaction on Oct. 24.

At Arkadiko, a lending protocol where users borrow against vault collateral, a roughly five-day vote ended two days early, giving a malicious contract authority over vault assets. People bought voting tokens shortly before the decisive vote, and the proposal took effect when the ballot closed.

The incidents expose different gaps between committing money, qualifying to vote, and executing an approved action. X100 tokens should be locked for a year, so a long token lock can impose a cost without delaying authority.

Meanwhile, a lengthy ballot can provide notice while still admitting late purchases. Neither automatically creates time to respond after a decision becomes executable.

X100’s locked stake bought immediate authority

X100’s Freezer contract holds frozen X tokens and supplies the stake used to rank candidates for its Senate. Its lock terms run for one, three, or five years, but Senate eligibility uses the amount currently frozen , without a minimum stake age.

In the first Oct. 24 attack, two helper contracts each froze 19,000.000001 X under the one-year term. They registered, entered the ranking, and supplied the two supporting votes that executed proposal 7. They completed the stake, votes, and execution in a single transaction.

The governance deadline offered no compulsory waiting period. While a proposal remained open, a majority of the currently ranked Senate seats could authorize execution. Holding two of the three seats gave the helpers enough power to act immediately.

The approved swap sent 400,000 treasury X into an attacker-created pool. The Freezer received only 35.675313 USDT, and the attacker then extracted tokens from that pool and sold X to obtain the cash used for repayment.

The stake stayed frozen while cash from the treasury extraction and token sale funded the repayment, so the attacker did not need to recover the purchased stake first.

The attack borrowed about 1.94 million USDT and repaid the principal plus its premium. After repayment, about 4.75 million USDT reached the first final recipient.

ChainBounty contributor Philippark reconciled 4.848 million USDT paid to three selected recipients . That subtotal excludes unsold X and its changing value, measuring selected payments.

The Freezer also retained a meaningful constraint: after execution, its X balance had to cover the total amount users had frozen. Protecting that quantity of locked principal did not protect external pool liquidity or the token’s market value.

Arkadiko’s proposal 12 was submitted at 20:35 UTC on Oct. 17 and executed at 16:04 UTC on Oct. 22. Its governance contract gave an outside proposer a voting interval of 720 Bitcoin blocks, commonly described as five days.

The rules required 0.25% of eligible DIKO supply to propose, 5% participation to reach quorum, and more yes than no votes. The supply calculation subtracted DIKO held in the initial-allocation contract.

Those thresholds and voting rules did not require token owners to have held tokens before the proposal. The proposing wallet made a swap at 15:03:46 UTC on Oct. 22 and a vote at 15:06:47. It committed about 4.573 million DIKO. The proposal closed with the same yes-vote total and zero no votes .

Bitquery estimates the voting-token purchases at roughly $51,000 . Its tracing also puts 77% of the STX sent toward the voting wallet as coming from the earlier StackSwap haul.

The attacker committed funds across multiple transactions and dates, so Arkadiko’s case differs materially from X100’s single-transaction borrowing and repayment. The late purchase was key because it became usable voting power during an already-open ballot.

When the ballot closed, the change executed. No separate waiting period existed between that decision and the contract receiving its authority.

X100’s attacker repaid a flash loan from theft proceeds while its stake stayed locked, and Arkadiko’s ballot accepted late token purchases.

An attacker still acquired two governance seats on X100, a token project with a Senate-governed treasury, and approved a treasury transaction and repaid a flash loan in a single blockchain transaction on Oct. 24.

Written by Felix Ng staff editor Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Felix Ng staff editor Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Discord is making public chats searchable on Google: How to opt out

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 Discord conversations on large public servers will soon reach audiences far beyond their communities, raising privacy concerns.

Discord is making a policy change that will make conversations from its largest public servers discoverable in search engines, including Google, raising privacy concerns among users whose conversations were previously confined to the platform.

The change applies to Discoverable Servers — communities with at least 1,000 members listed in Discord’s public directory that do not require an invitation to join.

From Nov. 16, every Discoverable Server will have a web page that may include summaries of public channel discussions. From mid-December, individual messages posted in eligible channels may appear in web search, Discord said Tuesday. Messages posted before the rollout will not be included, while usernames and avatars will be excluded from published messages.

Example of an individual message being shown online. Source: Discord

Discord said the shift of online communities from message boards to its servers had made useful answers harder to find. “This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this,” the company said.

The move has drawn criticism from users concerned about their conversations reaching an audience outside of their intended community, even if the servers are public in the first place.

Related: Starknet introduces wallet privacy feature for DeFi activity

Others welcomed the change, saying it could make useful answers easier to find. One user in Discord’s announcement thread called it “very much necessary,” while another said moving communities from forums to Discord had made their discussions harder to find through search.

The change could also affect cryptocurrency communities that use Discord for technical discussions, support and project announcements.

Cointelegraph found nearly 800 servers tagged “cryptocurrency,” around 1,400 tagged “trading” and more than 700 tagged “finance” in Discord’s public directory. Discord said there are over 63,000 total discoverable servers on its platform.

Users have until the message-sharing rollout begins in mid-December to opt out before their posts become eligible to appear online. Discord said the feature will be disabled by default for users in Australia, the EU, the European Economic Area, the UK, Canada, Brazil and South Korea. Teen users will also be excluded.

To opt out, users should go into User Settings > Data & Privacy and switch off “Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages.” The setting covers every Discoverable Server a user belongs to, according to Discord’s guidance .

How users can opt out of having their messages visible on web pages. Source: Discord

Users can also disable the feature after launch, but it only protects messages sent after the opt-out. Users who want an eligible message removed must delete it from Discord, and Discord warns that search engines may retain cached copies for some time.

Server administrators can also prevent messages from individual channels or entire servers from appearing on public web pages and in search results through Server Settings > Web Presence.

They can separately disable discussion summaries, which are scheduled to begin rolling out in November.
